Any link is external etymology, which is disallowed. This is decisive proof that same-root does not equal one meaning here and caps the root against a single nucleus.
nSr.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B derivational, C adversarial) converged on the same two-class result (one backing family + one unbridged PN class) and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade.

lqy.candidate_root_contribution: lqy encodes the JUNCTURE of two entities — one coming into direct contact/arrival with a counterpart — with the derivational form fixing the DIRECTION of that contact. Form I (laqiya) = a subject comes upon / into confrontation with an object (person, foe, God, or an incurred outcome); Forms VIII/VI = two parties mutually converge; Form III nominal/participle (liqāʾ, mulāqī, yulāqī) = the (chiefly eschatological) Encounter itself and the one who will meet; Form V (talaqqā) = accept/take up what reaches one; Form II (laqqā) = cause a person to receive an immaterial good. Form IV (alqā) is the productive causative of Form I — 'cause an object to reach/arrive at a target' → cast / throw / put down / place / project / deliver — bridged to the encounter core by its causative morphology, the pervasive ilā/fī/ʿalā-goal arrival frame, and transparent deliver-to-recipient tokens (alqā ilā X 'a word/book/peace'), even though its lexicalized center of gravity is 'cast/deliver', not 'meet'. This is one derivational family with morphologically distributed senses, not a single narrow gloss and not two unrelated homonyms.
lqy.plain_explanation: The root ل ق ي is about two things being brought into direct contact. Depending on the verb pattern, that contact is described from a different angle: you 'meet/come upon' someone or something (Form I); two sides 'converge' on each other (Forms VIII/VI); the noun names 'the Meeting', above all the future meeting with God (Form III); you 'receive/take up' what comes to you (Form V) or are 'made to receive' a gift like revelation or reward (Form II); and — as the causative — you 'cast, throw, put down, or deliver' an object so it reaches a place or a recipient (Form IV). The forms carry the grammar of who reaches whom; the shared idea is arrival-into-contact.
lqy.strongest_counterexample: 84:4:1:2 — wa-alqat mā fīhā wa-takhallat ('[the earth] cast out what is in it and emptied itself'): Form IV here is expulsion/ejection with the terminus OUT/AWAY and no counterpart or recipient, inverting rather than instantiating the two-entities-converge nucleus; it is absorbed only by the CAST class's 'directed projection including ejection', not by the encounter core, and it is reinforced by the Quran-internal interchange of alqā with qadhafa 'to hurl' in the same act (20:39, 20:87). This is the single occurrence that most strongly prevents collapsing the whole root into one 'meeting' gloss.
lqy.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, C) all read full coverage; A and B converged on MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE, and adversary C's homonymy challenge was weighed and localized to the recorded resistant occurrences rather than refuting the bridged family.

TwE.plain_explanation: Across all 129 occurrences the root ط و ع does not resolve to a single Quran-internal nucleus; it splits into two internally-coherent but mutually unbridged fields. (1) A WILLING-COMPLIANCE family (87 occ): obey (Form IV أطاع, 72×), be-obeyed (passive يُطاع and ADJ مُطاع), the willing-vs-coerced MODE (طوعًا, always the marked pole opposed to كرهًا), nominal obedience/assent (طاعة), voluntary supererogation (Form V تطوّع, N(V) المطّوّعين), and the causative make-willing (Form II 5:30). Its antonyms are عصى (of أطاع) and كره (of طوعًا). (2) A CAPACITY field (42 occ): Form X استطاع/يستطيع 'to have the power/means to accomplish X' — will-independent, carrying no antonym pair (simply negated), predicated even of God (5:112) and inanimate idols (36:75). No single occurrence bridges the two fields; the only link ('yielding'→'ability') is etymological/derivational, which the contract bars as semantic authority. The honest result is therefore a multi-class UNRESOLVED partition, not one meaning.
TwE.strongest_counterexample: 5:112 — هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ أَن يُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا مَآئِدَةً ('Is your Lord ABLE to send down a table?'): Form X predicates raw capability OF GOD, with zero possible notion of obedience or willing-yielding — falsifying any account that makes 'obey/comply' the root's core. Reinforced by 36:75 (idols لا يستطيعون نصرهم — brute incapacity, no will) and, decisively for the non-bridge, by 64:16 (فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ وَٱسْمَعُوا۟ وَأَطِيعُوا۟) where Form X supplies EXTENT (capacity) and Form IV supplies the ACT (compliance) side by side — the Quran uses them as two distinct things, not synonyms.
TwE.independent_verification: Lenses A, B, and C independently converged on the same two-class split with only an etymological (barred) link; adversary C additionally established that 64:16 distinguishes both senses in a single verse and 5:112 predicates capacity of God, blocking unification.

Twf.candidate_root_contribution: To move in an encircling / roundabout circuit — going round, about, or among a reference point or set — as opposed to linear goal-directed travel toward a destination. Case-government is internally regular: bi- = go round an axis/locus (22:29 bi-l-Bayt; 2:158 bi-himā), 'alā = circulate round/upon/among (52:24; 56:17; 76:19; 68:19), yuTaAfu bi- = be passed round / circulated with vessels (37:45; 43:71; 76:15), bayna…wa-bayna = driven to-and-fro between two poles (55:44). The sense includes the agentive nominal 'an encompassing visitation that comes round upon one' (68:19 TaA^}if min rabbik, bridged in-verse to the verb TaAfa). This account governs the verbal–participial derivational family (Form I TaAfa/yaTuwfu/yuTaAfu, Form V yaT~aw~afa, participles TaA^}if / TaA^}ifiyn, intensive Taw~a`f). It does NOT extend to the lexicalized nominal TaA^}ifa 'a portion/faction' (a partitive subset of a whole, carrying zero motion) nor to the lexicalized TuwfaAn 'overwhelming calamity/deluge'.
Twf.plain_explanation: When Twf appears as a verb or a moving-agent participle, it means to go around, circulate, or move about among/around something — pilgrims circling the House, youths circulating drink among reclining people, vessels being passed round, the damned driven back and forth between fire and scalding water, a calamity sweeping round a garden. It never means walking straight toward a goal. But the common noun TaA^}ifa ('a party / portion of a group') and the noun TuwfaAn ('the flood/plague') do not carry this going-around meaning at all; they are separate fixed words that only happen to share the root, so the root is not one single meaning.
Twf.strongest_counterexample: 6:156:7:1 'innamA unzila l-kitAbu 'alA TaA^}ifatayni min qablinA' — 'two [scripture-receiving] communities before us': a purely enumerated pair with zero motion, circuit, or encircling content. Reinforced decisively by 9:122:12:1 'min kulli firqatin minhum TaA^}ifatun' where TaA^}ifa stands in explicit apposition to firqa and is opposed to kAffa ('totality'), and by 49:9:2:1 / 8:7:5:2 (two believing parties fight / one of the two caravans). These prove that no single 'going-around' meaning can cover the corpus: the dominant TaA^}ifa class belongs to the faction/portion field, not the motion field.
Twf.independent_verification: Three independent lenses converged: Analyst A (bottom-up form/government), Analyst B (bridging-test), Adversary C (adversarial refutation). All three independently isolated the same motion nucleus, the same resistant TaA^}ifa class, and the same TuwfaAn residue, and all three proposed MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE with a multi-class structural verdict.

flH.candidate_root_contribution: flH is attested Quran-internally ONLY as the Form IV af'ala family (the finite verb aflaHa/yufliHu/tufliHu and its agent-noun al-mufliHun/al-mufliHin), and in this family it denotes, for a person(-class) subject and always intransitively, ATTAINING/COMING OUT WELL — settling into the aimed-at favorable end-state, coming out ahead. It names an outcome/achievement (the result the imperatives aim at), not an action, effort, or feeling; it is evaluative-total (the subject's whole standing) and binary/class-defining (one is of al-mufliHun or is denied it), never gradable, never transitive/causative, never concrete/agrarian. The moral, eschatological, or salvific value everywhere attached to it is supplied by the subject and context, NOT entailed by the lexeme.
flH.plain_explanation: Every one of the 40 occurrences is Form IV, in two shapes: 27 verbs and 13 active participles (al-mufliHun / al-mufliHin). Across all four grammatical deployments the meaning holds steady: perfect qad aflaHa = the good subject HAS come out well (believers 23:1, the self-purifier 87:14/91:9); negated lA yufliHu = the wrongdoer-class (mujrimun, Zalimun, kafirun, sAHir, liars-against-God) will NOT come out well; laAAallakum tufliHun = so that you MAY come out well (held out as the hoped-for result of taqwA, jihAd, dhikr, patience, shunning khamr/ribA); and al-mufliHun = the standing designation of those who have attained it. What varies is grammar and rhetorical polarity, not sense. The one sharp test, 20:64 (Pharaoh's sorcerers: 'and whoever gains the upper hand TODAY has aflaHa'), is worldly, time-bounded, and spoken by the condemned party, and the text rebuts it five verses later (20:69, 'the sorcerer does not yufliHu wherever he comes'). That token shows the bare word means only 'attain the aimed-at good outcome' — the salvation-coloring elsewhere is contextual, not lexical. Because the root never appears outside Form IV, this is honestly a claim about the Form-IV family, not about a deeper triangulated root sense.
flH.strongest_counterexample: 20:64:7:1 — wa-qad aflaHa l-yawma mani staAAlA ('and today whoever gains the upper hand has aflaHa'), spoken by Pharaoh's sorcerers. It is (a) worldly and non-eschatological, (b) voiced by the very class elsewhere told lA yufliHu, (c) about sheer domination (istaAAlA), and (d) explicitly time-bounded by al-yawma, with an in-narrative rebuttal at 20:69:13:1 (lA yufliHu l-sAHiru Haythu atA). It REFUTES any account that builds salvation/righteousness into the lexeme, but CONFIRMS the thin nucleus 'attain the aimed-at favorable outcome / come out ahead' — hence it is an adversarial boundary that bounds the gloss, not a resistant seam that breaks unity.
flH.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, and adversary C) all read all 40 occurrences and converged on the same nucleus and the same decisive token; the divergence was only on grade/scope, which is resolved here by bounding scope to the derivational family (REPRESENTATIVE/DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY) rather than by weakening the nucleus. Residual, non-falsifying caveat: distinctiveness from neighbour success-roots (fwz/njw/rbH) cannot be tested from this single-root packet and is left open in reopen_conditions.

*rr.plain_explanation: The geminate root ذ-ر-ر surfaces in the Quran only as nouns (form_inventory = {N:38}); there is no verb anywhere, so no process/action sense is attested. The 38 tokens split cleanly and without overlap into two lexicalized nominal classes that never co-occur, never gloss one another, and share no collocate or referent. Class A ذَرَّة (6 occ, surface *ar~apK) appears exclusively in the fixed idiom مِثْقَال ذَرَّة, denoting the smallest nameable quantity on a weight/magnitude scale used as a threshold-of-notice in divine reckoning (omniscience 10:61/34:3/34:22, justice 4:40, recompense 99:7-8); 10:61 and 34:3 themselves rank it between أَصْغَر and أَكْبَر, so it is a benchmark quantum, not the absolute minimum. Class B ذُرِّيَّة / ذُرِّيَّٰت (32 occ, surface *ur~iy~ap-/*ur~iy~a`t-) denotes progeny, the descending line issuing from a progenitor or stock, scalable from one child (3:38) to many, potentially trans-generational (6:84, 19:58). The only account that would unify 'smallest mote' with 'progeny' is the external etymology (a scatter/seed verb) which is barred by source policy and is attested for neither word in-corpus. Therefore the honest deliverable is two Quran-internally unbridged classes, not one root nucleus; each class is coherent on its own but no shared semantic contribution can be demonstrated.
*rr.strongest_counterexample: 34:3:17:1 (par. 10:61:27:1): مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ ... وَلَآ أَصْغَرُ مِن ذَٰلِكَ وَلَآ أَكْبَرُ — here the text itself defines ذَرَّة as a graded point on a magnitude continuum between 'smaller' and 'larger', a pure metrological term. This self-supplied frame is categorially incompatible with the living-descendant sense of ذُرِّيَّة (e.g. 3:38:11:1 ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً, a goodly child), and because the verse fixes its own semantics it cannot be re-read toward the progeny class. No semantic operation maps 'a unit of weight' onto 'a descendant', so this occurrence blocks any single narrow nucleus spanning both classes.
*rr.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each concluded, without coordination, that ذ-ر-ر hosts two unbridged lexicalized nominal classes and that a unified nucleus is not Quran-internally demonstrable.

Alw.plain_explanation: The 37 tokens tagged to root ا-ل-و do not form one semantic field. 34 of 37 are the fixed broken plural ءَالَآء ('the Lord's bestowed favors/bounties'), a lexicalized noun always in construct with the divine (رَبّ / ٱللَّه) and always the object of an acknowledgment verb — to be remembered (7:69, 7:74), not doubted (53:55), or not denied (the 31x Surah-55 refrain plus its 53:55 twin). The remaining 3 are finite verbs in three different forms with three different argument frames, all in the privative/withholding zone: يَأْلُونَ (Form I, 3:118) 'fall short / stint / spare no effort'; يُؤْلُونَ (Form IV, 2:226) 'swear a binding oath of conjugal abstention'; and يَأْتَلِ (Form VIII, 24:22), irreducibly ambiguous between 'swear not to give' and 'fall short of giving.' The noun (bestowed favor) and the verbs (withholding/stinting) sit at opposite poles of a notional giving axis, but the Quran nowhere links them: no shared collocation, no derivational base token, no occurrence bridging favor to swearing/falling-short. Because the bridge across the two classes is not Quran-internally demonstrated, the honest result is an unresolved, multi-class partition rather than a forced single nucleus. Each class is separately coherent (the noun cleanly, the verb only loosely across its own three forms), but no root-wide meaning survives.
Alw.strongest_counterexample: Juxtapose 2:226:2:1 يُؤْلُونَ مِن نِّسَآئِهِمْ ('those who swear to withhold from their wives') against 55:13:2:1 / 53:55:2:1 ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا/رَبِّكَ ('the bounties of your Lord'). A single nucleus must make 'swearing to withhold conjugal relations' and 'granted divine bounties' instances of one meaning — but they are opposite in direction of transfer (withholding vs. bestowing) and share zero Quran-internal collocational or morphological bridge. If the nucleus is 'favor/bounty' (the 92% reading), 2:226 disproves it; if the nucleus is 'binding withholding/restraint,' the ءَالَآء refrain disproves it. No single nucleus escapes both blocs; this pair is the decisive evidence that the QAC bucket is a homographic/derivational conflation, not a semantic unity.
Alw.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) converged on the same two-class partition and the same defeat of the unifying 'polarity' account; the aggregator re-opened the packet and confirmed all 37 word_refs, qac_pos/qac_verb_form values, and verse_texts.

bTl.candidate_root_contribution: bTl = being void of real standing / valid foundation / lasting effect — hence null and coming to nothing. The morphology tracks a clean argument-structure alternation on one nucleus: Form I intransitive baTala = 'become void, come to nothing' (7:118); Form IV causative abTala = 'render void, nullify' (10:81, 2:264, 47:33, 8:8); the substantive al-baaTil = 'that which has no reality/ground', lexicalized as the perishable, non-generative, non-penetrating counter-pole of al-Haqq (17:81, 34:49, 41:42, 21:18, 42:24). 'False' is a downstream specialization under the Haqq-contrast, not the superordinate; the causative applied to genuinely good acts (2:264 charities, 47:33 deeds) proves the core is efficacy/standing, not truth-value.
bTl.plain_explanation: Across all four morphological classes the root turns on one idea: lacking real substance so that a thing has no standing and comes to nothing. A deed can 'baTala' (become void, 7:118); God can 'abTala' magic, charity, or deeds (nullify them, 10:81/2:264/47:33); and 'al-baaTil' is the thing with no reality that vanishes when the real (al-Haqq) arrives — it is 'ever bound to vanish' (17:81), 'can neither originate nor restore' (34:49), is 'crushed' (21:18) and 'blotted out' (42:24). Decisively, 8:8 uses the root's own causative on its own noun — 'nullify the void' (yubTila l-baaTil) — bridging verb and substantive internally. Two peripheries strain the nucleus: the adverbial 'baaTilan' = 'in vain / to no end' (38:27, 3:191), a register shift that still bridges via 'no real purpose'; and, more seriously, the frozen juridical idiom 'akl al-amwaal bi-l-baaTil' = 'consuming wealth wrongfully' (2:188, 4:29, 4:161, 9:34), whose operative contrast is lawful/consensual acquisition, not truth or perishing — a resistant lexicalized sub-class that caps the grade.
bTl.strongest_counterexample: In the juridical collocation akl al-amwaal bi-l-baaTil (2:188:5:3, 4:29:8:3, 4:161:9:3, 9:34:12:3) the operative contrast is lawful/consensual acquisition — 'illaa an takuwna tijaaratan ʿan taraaDin' (4:29) — not al-Haqq, nor perishing/non-endurance. The activated axis is legitimacy of title/entitlement; 2:188 routes the wrongful wealth 'ilaa l-Hukkaam' (a legal-procedural frame). The text condemns the taking as wrongful/without valid basis and never marks the wealth as void or as coming to nothing, so the root's distinctive 'perishes before the real' content is NOT demonstrated for this class; it fits only the thinnest 'lacking valid ground' abstraction. This is a coherent, frozen, four-occurrence lexicalized nominal sub-class.
bTl.independent_verification: All three lenses (A bottom-up, B top-down, C adversarial) independently converged on MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE and independently identified the bi-l-baaTil juridical idiom as the grade-capping resistant class; packet word_refs, forms, and verse_texts re-verified against b_54_l.json by the aggregator.

fdy.candidate_root_contribution: fdy = the provision of a valued substitute (a stand-in / price, syntactically the bi-marked slot) IN PLACE OF a person or a person's incurred liability, in order to (seek to) release or exempt them from a binding claim — punishment, captivity, or a marital bond. The substitution-for-discharge core holds across all four forms (I redeems another 37:107; III mutual ransom of captives 2:85; VIII self-ransom, all 7; N the substitute-object/transaction), with morphology carrying only the direction/beneficiary, not the meaning. Two invariants are Quran-internal: (1) the substitute is near-obligatorily bi-marked (bihi, bi-dhibhin, bi-banihi), and (2) the claim/peril escaped is min-marked or contextual (min 'adhab, usara, the bond in 2:229). The account is efficacy-NEUTRAL: it names the offer of a substitute, decoupled from acceptance. This preferred nucleus covers 11/13; it does NOT cleanly extend to the lexicalized ritual nominal fidyah (2:184/2:196), where no person is imperiled or released and only a devotional/ritual obligation is discharged — a coherent resistant sub-class that caps the grade below STRONG.
fdy.plain_explanation: The root fdy is about giving something of value as a stand-in to buy someone's release from a hold on them — a punishment, being a captive, or a marriage bond. What is always foregrounded is the thing offered in exchange (marked by 'bi-'): earth-full of gold, one's own sons, a sacrificial animal, or the returned dowry. A striking Quran-internal fact is that the word does not imply the ransom works: six of seven self-ransom cases and 57:15 are refused or hypothetical, while 2:229 (a wife redeeming herself from marriage) and 2:85 (ransoming captives) and 37:107 (God redeeming the son) do take effect. Grammar sets the direction (redeem oneself vs. redeem another), not the meaning. The one place the picture stretches is the ritual 'fidyah' of 2:184/2:196 — feeding a poor person instead of fasting, or fasting/charity/sacrifice for shaving in ihram — where nobody is a captive and nobody is freed; there it means a prescribed substitute discharging a ritual duty. Because that nominal use is a coherent, lexicalized departure from the ransom-a-person center, the finding is honestly graded MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE rather than a single root-wide claim.
fdy.strongest_counterexample: 2:184:17:1 — 'fidyatun ta'amu miskin' (a fidyah: feeding a poor person). Here there is no captor, no penalty escaped, no bond, and no PERSON released — only an alternative act discharging a ritual/devotional obligation (feeding instead of fasting). It resists the distinctive 'ransom a person from penalty/captivity/bond' nucleus and can be absorbed only by retreating to the over-broad 'a substitute given in lieu of X to discharge a claim,' which the methodology disqualifies as fitting everything. 2:196 ('fa-fidyatun min siyamin aw sadaqatin aw nusuk', with sadaqah listed as a sub-option within fidyah, so fidyah != charity) reinforces this as a coherent lexicalized ritual sub-class rather than an isolated outlier.
fdy.independent_verification: Convergence of two independent lenses (A, C) on MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE with the same resistant sub-class; the third lens (B) reached STRONG only via a shared-root/schema bridge that the methodology forbids, so it does not license PASSED.

nSH.candidate_root_contribution: nSH = genuine, unfeigned good-faith orientation directed toward the proper good of / what is due to a party — surfacing (for human recipients) as sincere counsel, beneficial warning, or devoted caretaking, and (toward God) as loyal sincere devotion; by intensive-adjectival extension, the wholehearted genuineness of a (Godward) directed act.
nSH.plain_explanation: Across 12 of 13 occurrences the root construes its object through benefactive لِ (lakum, lahu, laka, lakumā, li-llāh), marking an act oriented FOR a party's good rather than performed ON a patient. It is not 'advice-content' (28:12 is devoted nursing of an infant; 9:91 is fidelity toward God, whom one cannot advise), and it is explicitly listed alongside — hence distinct from — message-conveyance (balāgh: 7:62, 7:79, 7:93) and from trustworthiness (amīn, listed separately at 7:68). It names the agent's good-faith stance, not the outcome: it can fail to benefit (11:34), be unloved (7:79), or be falsely sworn (7:21, 12:11). The lone intensive adjective naSūH (66:8), predicated of repentance with no beneficiary and no لِ, deploys only the genuineness component onto an act and forms a resistant lexicalized sub-class.
nSH.strongest_counterexample: 66:8:8:1 «تَوْبَةً نَّصُوحًا» — the sole ADJ (faʿūl intensive), sole non-لِ, sole occurrence with no directed party: nSH qualifies an act (repentance), not a recipient-directed relation. It resists the benefactive-directedness core and is accommodated only by abstracting to the bare 'genuineness/wholeheartedness of a (Godward) act', a bridge no verse in the packet forces. This resistant lexicalized adjectival sub-class caps the root claim below STRONG.
nSH.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, C) converged on the same partition, the same resistant seam (66:8), and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade.

wqt.candidate_root_contribution: wqt = the fixing/designation of a determinate, appointed temporal boundary — a set point OR a bounded term at/for which something occurs. It supplies the appointedness/fixedness of a time, not time-as-flow or duration-as-such, not the event/entity itself, and not place.
wqt.plain_explanation: Across all 13 occurrences the root marks a time that has been fixed or appointed, never generic elapsing time. The base noun waqt is a determinate moment (the 'known time' of respite in 15:38=38:81; the hidden-but-fixed time of the Hour in 7:187). The mif'al noun miqat is an appointed time/term (the Day of Decision in 44:40/78:17; the gathering of a known day in 26:38/56:50; Moses's appointment in 7:143/7:155; a term 'completed at forty nights' in 7:142). The plural mawaqit are calendrical time-markers (2:189, the crescents). The participle mawqut is prayer 'made time-fixed' (4:103). The sole verb, Form II passive uqqitat (77:11), is 'the messengers are assigned their appointed time.' The common core is demarcation/appointment of a time; whether that time is a point or a span, a one-off decree or a recurring marker, is supplied by context, not by the root.
wqt.strongest_counterexample: 7:142:8:1 — «فَتَمَّ مِيقَٰتُ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً». Because the miqat is 'completed' (tamma) and quantified as forty nights, it behaves as a bounded term/duration rather than a punctual instant. This blocks the narrower gloss 'fixed appointed moment/deadline' and forces the nucleus to be stated as 'fixed point OR bounded term,' reducing its discriminating sharpness. It refines the account rather than breaking it.
wqt.independent_verification: Cross-lens: Analysts A and B independently derived the same nucleus and graded STRONG; adversary C independently confirmed no contradicting occurrence but argued the nominal-dominant, formulaic, hapax-anchored, abstraction-leaning evidence caps below STRONG. The aggregator adopts C's calibrated ceiling.

$qw.candidate_root_contribution: ش ق و = to be or become in the NEGATIVE POLE of one's condition — badly-off, hard-pressed, wretched, ill-fated: the privation of ease/wellbeing, the explicit counter-pole of سعادة/سعيد (fixed verse-internally at 11:105 شَقِىّ ↔ سَعِيد). The root is uniformly negative-valenced and supplies only this adverse-lot nucleus; the DOMAIN of the privation — worldly toil/want, settled eschatological ruin, unanswered supplication, or graceless character — is supplied by context/collocation, not by the root itself.
$qw.plain_explanation: Across all 12 occurrences the root marks the bad end of a person's lot: being wretched, hard-pressed, or ill-fated, as opposed to being fortunate and at ease (سعيد). The Qur'an itself sets the opposite pole (11:105 pairs شَقِىّ with سَعِيد). What KIND of misfortune it is comes from the surrounding words, not the root: physical toil and want when Adam is warned of leaving the Garden (20:117, glossed by 20:118-119 hunger/thirst/nakedness/heat) and when the Prophet is told the Qur'an was not sent 'to distress you' (20:2); the wretched who reach the Fire (11:106, and the superlative 'most-wretched' at 92:15/87:11); an ingrained wretched-state (23:106 شِقْوَة); a graceless character coupled with tyranny (19:32 جَبَّار شَقِيّ); and being 'left empty-handed' in prayer (19:4, 19:48). The last of these is a fixed twice-used idiom carrying specific 'fruitless-supplication' content the bare root does not supply, which is why the account cannot be graded above MODERATE.
$qw.strongest_counterexample: 20:2 لِتَشْقَىٰ is addressed to the Prophet as this-worldly burden/distress with no moral fault and no Fire, disproving any damnation/wickedness nucleus; the eschatological content in 11:106/92:15 is supplied by explicit فِى ٱلنَّارِ / يَصْلَىٰهَا, not by the root. Symmetrically, forcing a 'mere physical toil' gloss breaks on 11:105 (↔ سَعِيد) and 92:15 (ٱلْأَشْقَى + burning). This two-sided pressure is what forces the broad adverse-lot nucleus rather than either narrow pole.
$qw.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, C) all affirm the single negative-pole nucleus; two of three (A, C) independently grade MODERATE and identify the same resistant material (19:4/19:48 دعاء seam; 20:2 vs 11:106 domain split), and B's own honest fallback is MODERATE.

Hsr.candidate_root_contribution: In its dominant lexicalized nominal shape — the faʿlah noun ḥasrah / plural ḥasarāt (9 of 12 occurrences) — the root names anguished, terminal regret felt over an irrecoverable loss or a neglected obligation: the self's grieving reaction to what can no longer be undone. It is regularly directed by ʿalā + the thing regretted (39:56 ʿalā mā farraṭtu, 6:31 ʿalā mā farraṭnā, 36:30 ʿalā l-ʿibād, 69:50 ʿalā l-kāfirīn) or seated fī qulūb (3:156), and is tied to irreversibility (19:39 the Day when qudiya l-amr; 2:167 deeds shown back with no return). It denotes neither the loss itself nor generic sorrow. This claim is scoped to that lexicalized class; a separate depletion/exhaustion class (17:29, 21:19, 67:4) is present in the root and is NOT Quran-internally bridged to it.
Hsr.plain_explanation: For its most common form, the noun ḥasrah, this root means the bitter, too-late regret you feel over something lost or neglected that can never be put right — the anguish of 'if only,' not just sadness and not the loss itself. A separate handful of words from the same root (a worn-out eye, tireless angels, a man left destitute) instead mean being drained or worn out physically, with no regret in them at all. The Quran never uses one word that carries both meanings, so we make the confident claim only about the ḥasrah 'regret' family and record the 'depletion' words as an unbridged second class.
Hsr.strongest_counterexample: 21:19:13:1 yastaḥsirūn (wa-lā yastaḥsirūn, of the angels): the one finite verb of the root, predicated of sinless beings for whom regret is impossible, negated in parallel with yastakbirūn (pride) — its sense is unmistakably 'grow weary / flag / become spent,' pure depletion of stamina with zero regret. Reinforced by 67:4 ḥasīr (the strained sight returns worn out) and 17:29 maḥsūr (one sits stripped/destitute after over-spending). These three disprove any attempt to read the whole root as 'regret' and force recognition of a depletion class that the ḥasrah-regret claim does not and should not cover.
Hsr.independent_verification: All three independent analyses (A, B, adversary C) reached the same two-class split, the same unbridged status, and the same REPRESENTATIVE/MODERATE grade; C additionally verified that sense is confounded with morphology so no minimal pair exists to test unity.

TfA.candidate_root_contribution: TfA (attested only as Form IV causative أَفْعَلَ) = to cause a burning or shining source to cease being alight — to quench/extinguish a fire or a light. The object is invariably a luminous-or-combusting referent (نَار once, نُور twice) and the verb targets that active flaming/radiant state, not the substance, source, or agent behind it. The lexeme is outcome-neutral: whether the extinguishing succeeds is supplied by the surrounding frame, not by the root.
TfA.plain_explanation: Across all three occurrences the root means 'put out' — to make a fire or a light stop burning/shining. In 5:64 God actually puts out a war-fire the enemies kindle (paired antonymically with أَوْقَدُوا 'kindle'). In 61:8 and 9:32 disbelievers merely wish to blow out God's light with their mouths, and are explicitly thwarted (مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ / يُتِمَّ نُورَهُ). The action of 'quenching' is identical in all three; only the object domain (physical fire vs. divine light) and the outcome (accomplished vs. frustrated) differ, and both of those differences are carried by context, not by the verb.
TfA.strongest_counterexample: 61:8 (≈ 9:32): the object نُورَ ٱللَّهِ is abstract divine light, not combustible matter, and it is the majority-by-count class, inviting a re-read as 'suppress/nullify divine truth' rather than 'extinguish a flame.' It does not resist the nucleus: the instrument بِأَفْوَٰهِهِمْ (mouths/breath) invokes the prototypical scene of blowing out a flame, and the act denotes cessation of an existing luminous manifestation — the same core as 5:64. It caps breadth and independence (figurative + formulaic + count-dominant), not coherence.
TfA.independent_verification: All three lenses (A, B, C) independently reached the same nucleus, grading, and rejection of the abstract competitor; adversary C explicitly ran and reported the two failed disproof lines.

brH.candidate_root_contribution: brH = to depart from / leave off / discontinue a maintained position or activity. It surfaces spatially as a full transitive verb 'leave (a place)' (12:80) and aspectually as a grammaticalized continuance-verb (sister of kana) 'cease / leave off (a state or ongoing act)' (18:60, 20:91). In the attested corpus every token is negated and closed by a hatta terminus, so the familiar 'remain steadfast until X' reading is a compositional product of the negator operating on 'depart/cease', not a positive contribution of the root itself.
brH.plain_explanation: All three occurrences of b-r-H are first-person imperfect verbs, all negated (lan/la), and all followed by a hatta 'until' clause naming an end event. The root itself means 'to depart / leave off / stop doing'. Because it is always negated here, the whole phrase means 'I/we will not leave off ... until ...', i.e. a vow to stay put or keep going until a boundary. In 12:80 it takes a concrete place-object ('the land'), so it is a plain motion verb 'depart'; in 18:60 and 20:91 it works like a helper verb of continuance ('will not cease'), with 20:91 attaching a state ('being devoted', 'akifin') rather than a place. The persistence sense belongs to the negation, not to the root.
brH.strongest_counterexample: 20:91 نَّبْرَحَ governs the stative predicate عَٰكِفِينَ (a posture/devotional condition, not a place) while the devotees physically stay put, so برح here cannot mean locative departure and forces the abstract 'leave off/cease a maintained state' nucleus; conversely 12:80 أَبْرَحَ ٱلْأَرْضَ takes a concrete accusative place-object that a bare aspectual 'not-cease' auxiliary cannot host — the two poles mutually resist, and neither reduces to the other without importing the classical 'depart-place / cease-state' bridge, which is not demonstrated Quran-internally (no affirmative and no shared-construction control token exists).
brH.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (bottom-up A, nucleus B, adversary C) converged on the same nucleus, the same two-construction split, and the same MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE grade; adversary C's splitting account was tested and could not be refuted Quran-internally, which is exactly why distinctiveness_ok=false.

ftl.candidate_root_contribution: Quran-internally the root ف ت ل survives only as the single frozen accusative noun فَتِيلًا (fatiylFA), a lexicalized minimal-quantity token — the smallest conceivable measure — deployed exclusively as the accusative of measure/specification (tamyiz) under a negated passive of ظ ل م to assert that no wronging occurs 'in the slightest'. The word-function claim (frozen minimal-measure token under negated ظلم) is defensible across 3/3 occurrences; the concrete referent and any productive verbal root nucleus (e.g. 'twist/thread/fibre') are NOT recoverable from Quran-internal evidence.
ftl.plain_explanation: This root appears in the Quran as exactly one word, فَتِيلًا, three times, and always in the same phrase: 'they/you are not wronged (by even) a fatil'. In every case it names the tiniest possible amount, used to stress that God's justice leaves out nothing at all. Because the word never appears as a verb, is never described, and is never used positively, the Quran itself never tells us what a fatil physically is or what action the root names — so the underlying root meaning cannot be recovered from the text; only the frozen word-function can.
ftl.strongest_counterexample: There is NO internal occurrence that resists the word-function account — and that is itself the adversarial weakness, not a strength. All three tokens are the identical frozen accusative فَتِيلًا in the identical 'لا يُظْلَمُون فَتِيلًا' construction, so the evidence base is homogeneous with zero morphological or contextual diversity: no possible internal datum could disprove a proposed root sense. Per contract, this non-resistance is the absence of a test, not the passing of one (CONSISTENT != established; absence of resistance != proof). Consequently any promotion from the word/idiom claim to a distinctive root-nucleus claim is unsupported, and any 'twist/thread' content would require forbidden external sources.
ftl.independent_verification: All three lenses (A, B, C) independently reached the same inventory, the same single-class functional reading, and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE cap with root nucleus UNRESOLVED; adversary C explicitly identified the unfalsifiability-by-homogeneity that blocks a PASSED falsification.

j*E.candidate_root_contribution: The concrete count-noun جِذْع / pl. جُذُوع denoting the rigid, upright, load-bearing woody trunk/bole of the palm — the standing structural body one is driven to and leans against (19:23), grips and shakes to transmit force so fruit drops (19:25), and fastens a body onto (20:71). It is a PART of the palm, distinct from the whole tree and from its fruit, and neutral to whether the palm is living or fruit-bearing. No abstract, verbal, or metaphorical root sense is Quran-attested.
j*E.plain_explanation: All three occurrences are the same noun, differing only in number (singular جِذْع twice, broken plural جُذُوع once). In every token it is bound in construct to the palm (النخلة / النخل) and names the tree's rigid vertical woody trunk: the thing Maryam is driven toward and can lean on, the body she shakes so ripe dates fall, and the upright post Pharaoh threatens to crucify the magicians upon. Three different physical uses — lean-against, grasp-and-shake, affix-body-to — all presuppose one and the same property: a stiff, weight-bearing vertical column. The sense is scene-neutral, appearing identically in divine provision and in tyrannical cruelty.
j*E.strongest_counterexample: 20:71 (فِى جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ) uses جِذْع as a bare crucifixion-post in the Pharaoh/magicians scene — different narrative, plural morphology, and a functional shift from part-of-a-living-palm (19:23–25) to instrument of execution. It does not break unity: the referent is still the palm's woody upright column, and the difference is contextual use, not lexical meaning. Its real evidential value is as a negative boundary — it disproves any richer 'living/fruiting stem' account and confirms the bare 'upright woody bole' nucleus that is neutral to whether the palm is living or fruit-bearing.
j*E.independent_verification: Three independent analyses (Lens A, Lens B, Adversary C) each ran the refutation and converged on the same narrow account and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE ceiling, each citing the same distinctiveness limitation.

kbt.candidate_root_contribution: A divinely-inflicted defeat that brings God's active opponents low — checking/thwarting their aim and abasing them — while leaving them alive (explicitly short of destroying or killing them).
kbt.plain_explanation: Across all three verbal tokens (Form I, active and passive), k-b-t names something God does to those who oppose Him and His Messenger: it brings them low. In 3:127 the imperfect active يَكْبِتَهُمْ is set by أَوْ against لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفًا ('cut off a portion'), i.e. it is the non-lethal alternative to destroying a group, and its result-clause فَيَنقَلِبُوا۟ خَآئِبِينَ shows survivors turning back thwarted/empty-handed. In 58:5 the two passives كُبِتُوا۟ / كُبِتَ assert a recurring pattern ('as those before them were') against the muḥāddūn, adjacent to a separately-promised عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ. The single field account 'humiliating bring-low of God's opponents, short of destruction' covers all three; whether the finer emphasis is dynamic thwarting (3:127) or settled abasement (58:5) is not arbitrated by the corpus.
kbt.strongest_counterexample: 3:127:7:1 يَكْبِتَهُمْ is coordinated by أَوْ with لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفًا and yields فَيَنقَلِبُوا۟ خَآئِبِينَ — a dynamic, non-lethal battlefield thwarting whose foregrounded content is frustration/repulse, not disgrace. This decisively refutes any 'kbt = kill/destroy' gloss (establishing the ≠ annihilation boundary) and simultaneously resists an 'abasement-primary' nucleus, since the salient outcome here is being foiled and turned back, not being disgraced.
kbt.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B structural, C adversarial) converged on the same field account, the same ≠ kill boundary, and the same thwart-vs-abase underdetermination and MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade.

E*b.plain_explanation: The consonantal skeleton ع-ذ-ب hosts two Quran-internally UNBRIDGED classes, not one nucleus. Class A (371/373): the punishment/torment family عَذَاب (noun, 322) + عَذَّبَ / يُعَذِّب (verb form II, 41) + مُعَذِّب/مُعَذَّب (participles form II, 8) = the infliction of intense, painful, humiliating suffering on a subject by an authority, characteristically punitive; welded by cognate-object syntax (عَذَّبْنَٰهَا عَذَابًا نُّكرًا, 65:8) and by systematic antonymy with mercy/forgiveness. Class B (2/373): عَذْب (fa'l noun/adjective, 25:53:6:1 & 35:12:5:1) = sweet, palatable fresh water, opposed to مِلْح أُجَاج (salty-bitter). The two share ONLY the radicals: different derivational pattern, zero shared collocate, zero co-occurrence, and OPPOSITE affective valence (painful vs. pleasant). No Quran-internal thread bridges them, so the honest root-level result is a partition, not a single meaning. Meaning is carried by the derivational form, not by the radicals.
E*b.strongest_counterexample: هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ (25:53:6:1; and عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ سَآئِغٌ شَرَابُهُ 35:12:5:1) — 'sweet, fresh water, pleasant to drink,' explicitly paired against مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ. This single token is the exact affective inverse of painful عَذَاب and disproves ANY unified single-nucleus (or 'universal') reading of the root ع-ذ-ب: no account of 'infliction of painful suffering' can absorb 'delicious drinkable water,' and no morphological or collocational thread links the two anywhere in the 373 occurrences.
E*b.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B independent, C adversarial) over full 373/373 coverage converged on the identical two-class partition with zero Quran-internal bridge.

mwt.candidate_root_contribution: mwt denotes the LIFELESS condition - the state of being without hayah - standing in systematic paradigmatic opposition to the root h-y-y (life/living). It is anchored not by any external gloss but by invariant Quran-internal antonymy: yuhyi wa-yumit, al-hayy/al-mayyit, al-ahya'/al-amwat (35:22), mahyahum wa-mamatuhum (45:21), la yamutu fiha wa-la yahya (20:74). Morphology, not the root, supplies argument structure: Form I (yamutu/mata) = an entity's intransitive passage INTO the lifeless state (undergoer-subject, never causative); Form IV (yumit/amata) = an agent (canonically God) putting into it; the nominals name the state/onset-event (mawt), its countable instance (mawtah/mamat), or the entity in it (mayyit, mawta, amwat). The dietary maytah (carrion) is a lexicalized nominal specialization.
mwt.plain_explanation: The root mwt is about being without life, defined against its opposite root 'to live'. Whether it is a human, a barren land, a seed, or an idol, the thing called 'dead' is simply on the non-living side of the life/death pair. The verb shapes carry the rest of the meaning: the plain (Form I) verb means an entity itself passes into that lifeless state and never takes an object, while the causative (Form IV) verb means someone - in the Quran, God - makes something die. Nouns name the death-event, the lifeless state, or the dead ones. The one specialized use is 'maytah', a legal food-law term for carrion (an animal that died on its own), which adds a prohibition/impurity meaning the plain root does not have.
mwt.strongest_counterexample: 2:28:5:1 kuntum amwatan fa-ahyakum ('you were dead, then He gave you life') places the mawt-state PRIOR to life, so nothing living had ceased; reinforced by 16:21:1:1 (idols amwat ghayr ahya', never alive) and 40:11:3:1 (amattana ithnatayn, two deaths). This refutes any 'cessation of prior life' gloss and forces the nucleus to the lifeless CONDITION (negative pole of h-y-y), not a termination event.
mwt.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B unity, C adversary) converged on the same nucleus, the same Form I/IV split, and the same sole resistant sub-class (maytah), with no cross-lens disagreement on grading (all proposed MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE).

Sdq.candidate_root_contribution: In its veracity family (Forms I, II, the abstract sidq, the intensive siddiq, and the elative asdaq: ~128/155), s-d-q = the conformity of a word - a claim, report, promise, prediction, or the revealed message - to reality; derivationally, being the person or proposition that so conforms (opposite of kadhib), and, in Form II, the factitive act of affirming/attesting/making such a word conform to reality. This account is representative of the dominant family only; it does NOT reach the almsgiving/gift field or the frozen 'friend' lexeme.
Sdq.plain_explanation: The core of this root is truth as correspondence: a statement, promise or vision that matches the facts, or a person whose word matches reality - the standing opposite of lying. The Quran extends this in a regular way: to keep or make-good a promise (bringing reality into line with one's word), and in the 'saddaqa' form to affirm or confirm something as true (scripture 'confirming' earlier scripture). But the same consonants also carry two senses the Quran never links back to truth: giving - alms, charity, remitting a debt or blood-money, and the bridal gift - and simply 'friend'. Because the text itself lists 'the truthful' and 'the almsgivers' side by side as different virtues (33:35), we report a strong core for the truth family and treat giving and friend as separate, unbridged classes rather than forcing them into one meaning.
Sdq.strongest_counterexample: 4:4 'saduqatihinna nihlatan' (the obligatory bridal gift) - a root-nominal denoting a marriage payment with no assertoric, fulfillment, or faith content, unassimilable to veracity by any Quran-internal step. It is backed by the whole almsgiving field, of which 9:60 'innama al-sadaqatu lil-fuqara'' is representative (a fiscal distribution category), and by 26:101 'wa-la sadiqin hamim' (friend). These defeat any claim that the root is semantically unified around truth. The sharpest strain INSIDE the family is 37:105 'saddaqta al-ru'ya' (Form II used for 'fulfilled the vision'), which collapses the II-declarative vs I-fulfil boundary but remains within the correspondence nucleus.
Sdq.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) converged on the same partition, the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade, and the same resistant classes.

dwn.candidate_root_contribution: dun is a relational positioner: it fixes a reference point R (always the superior/primary term, explicit or 'dhalika') and locates the marked item on the NOT-R side of R -- short of R, on the near side of R, or to the exclusion of R. dun itself carries none of 'god', 'worship', 'false', 'hostility', or 'negation'; those come from the matrix verbs/nouns (ya'budun, yad'un, ittakhadhu, awliya', alihah) and from surrounding ma/la. Context selects the pole: a scale -> 'lesser than / short of'; space/time -> 'on the near side of / before'; a choice-set -> 'other than / instead of / to the exclusion of'.
dwn.plain_explanation: The root shows up in the Quran only as the little relational word dun (accusative duna, 9x; genitive after min, min duni, 135x) -- never as a verb, participle, or verbal noun. Its one job is to place something relative to a benchmark R and say it does not reach, does not include, or is set apart from R. On a scale that reads 'less than' (the lesser punishment short of the greater, 32:21; speech below loudness, 7:205); in space it reads 'on the near side of' (a cover this side of the sun, 18:90; a people short of the two barriers, 18:93); in a choice it reads 'instead of / to the exclusion of' (men instead of women, 27:55; allies to the exclusion of the believers, 3:28). The famous 'besides Allah' phrase is just this last pole with R = God; the idolatry lives in the verbs, not in dun.
dwn.strongest_counterexample: 55:62:2:1 wa-min duni-hima jannatani: the second pair of Gardens is ADDED alongside the first pair, not put in its place and not ranked below it, so dun here resists both the exclusion pole ('instead of') and the scalar refinement ('lesser than'); only the bare positional relation ('on the other side of the reference pair') survives.
dwn.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, C) each read all 144 occurrences and all 9 LOC cases in full and converged on the same nucleus, the same competitor rejection, and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade with overlapping resistant occurrences (55:62 flagged by B and C; 48:27 by A; 23:63 by A and B).

jmE.candidate_root_contribution: The bringing (or coming) of multiple distinct entities into a single collected whole - aggregation/assembly-into-one, and its result/state (a gathering, host, accumulation, junction, or the totalizing 'all-as-one'). The root supplies togetherness/aggregation only; it does not itself supply purpose, valency, agentivity, or moral colour.
jmE.plain_explanation: Across all 129 occurrences one nucleus recurs: many things brought into one collection. It generates the concrete verbs (gather people, wealth, bones, two seas' junction, a scheme), the reflexive 'assemble', the nouns (host, junction, Day of Gathering, the Gatherer), and - grammaticalized - the totalizer jamiʿ ('all together') and the emphatic ajmaʿin ('every last one'). This 'collection-into-one' account is narrower and strictly more generative than 'totality', because 'totality' cannot produce 'gather his bones' or 'the junction of the two seas', whereas 'collection' produces both the verbs and the quantifier. The root's Quran-internal contrastive field is decisive: it stands against shatta / ashtat / tafarraqu / thubat (scattered/dispersed/sub-groups). Two coherent departures keep the judgment honest: Form IV ajmaʿa lexicalizes to 'firmly resolve upon a course' (governing amr / an-clause, in plotting frames), and jamiʿ/ajmaʿin (~61% of tokens) are grammaticalized totalizers with the gathering-act bleached.
jmE.strongest_counterexample: 12:15:4:2 wa-ajmaʿu an yajʿaluhu: Form IV governs a purposive an-clause (a decided action), not a set of co-located entities; Form I in this packet never takes an an-clause, so Form IV carries a distinct argument structure and a specialized 'settle/firmly resolve upon a course' sense.
jmE.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A constructive, B derivational-family, C adversarial) converged on the same nucleus, the same Form IV resistance, and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade.

jbl.plain_explanation: The 41 occurrences of ج ب ل split, along an exact morphological seam, into two Quran-internally UNBRIDGED classes. Class A (39/41), the non-geminate stem jabal/jibāl, denotes a mountain — a massive, elevated, firmly-founded rock-mass, deployed as the corpus's benchmark of magnitude and fixity across creation/stabilization, eschatological dissolution, and theophany/worship registers. Class B (2/41), the geminate stem jibill- (jibillah), denotes a large created multitude/generation of people, with no geological sense. Every non-mountain token is geminate and every mountain token is not; the morphology tracks the semantic split with zero exceptions. No occurrence uses jibāl for people or jibill- for terrain, and no verse bridges the two. The only thing joining them is the QAC root label, an etymological assignment, not a Quran-internal semantic demonstration; adopting it as a bridge would import a forbidden external lexical prior. Because two senses share a skeleton with no in-corpus bridge, the honest result is a multi-class UNRESOLVED partition rather than a forced single nucleus. (Note: Class A considered alone is a strong, distinctive, adversarially-clean lexeme — but that is a class-scoped observation, not a root-level nucleus.)
jbl.strongest_counterexample: 36:62:4:1 «وَلَقَدْ أَضَلَّ مِنكُمْ جِبِلًّا كَثِيرًا»: the governing verb أَضَلَّ (led astray), the partitive مِنكُمْ (of you), and the quantifier كَثِيرًا (a great number) make the referent a numerous body of persons, and the stem is morphologically geminate (jibil~FA). A mountain sense is impossible, not merely strained. Corroborated by 26:184:4:3 «خَلَقَكُمْ وَٱلْجِبِلَّةَ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ», where jibillah is an object of khalaqa paired with 'you' and 'the former ones'. This decisively blocks any single-nucleus unification of the root.
jbl.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, C) converged on the same morphologically-marked, unbridged two-class partition, with the adversary explicitly returning RESISTANT/UNRESOLVED for the single-nucleus hypothesis.

mlA.plain_explanation: The 40 occurrences of م ل ا split into two Quran-internally coherent but mutually unbridged classes. Class A (10 occ: Form I verbs, a Form VIII verb, the passive, the active participle مَالِئُون, and the verbal noun مِلْء) means 'bring/reach a bounded interior to its full capacity with a content' — Hell filled with jinn and humans, bellies with food, the sky with guards, a person with terror, the earth as a measure of gold. Class B (30 occ: the lexicalized noun ٱلْمَلَأ in case/definiteness/possessive variants, incl. the heavenly ٱلْمَلَإِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ) means 'the eminent leading assembly/council that speaks, deliberates, and decides for a people or ruler.' No verse predicates filling of the mala', and no fill-word denotes a council; the shared particle مِن plays opposite roles (content-partitive in A vs. group-partitive in B). Any 'fullness -> the full/eminent body' bridge exists only in external etymology, which the source policy forbids. The honest root-level result is therefore that the packet does not license a single nucleus: two classes, no Quran-internal bridge.
mlA.strongest_counterexample: 27:38:3:2 — قَالَ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ أَيُّكُمْ يَأْتِينِى بِعَرْشِهَا: a vocative direct address to persons asked 'which of you will bring me her throne?' There is no container, content, capacity, or quantity; no Class-A fill/full/a-fill-of sense can be substituted without nonsense. This decisively resists any unified 'fullness' nucleus. The would-be bridge, 26:34:2:3 قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُ ('to the assembly around him'), fails on inspection: حَوْلَهُ is a locative ظرف that places the persons, never a م ل ا fill-word, so the 'they fill the space around the ruler' reading imports external etymology the text does not state.
mlA.independent_verification: All three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) independently reached the identical two-class split and independently rejected the fullness-unification on Quran-internal grounds.

blw.candidate_root_contribution: blw — to subject a person or thing to a decisive imposed experience (whether by good or by ill) that draws out and makes its true condition manifest, so it can be discriminated, known, or recorded. The probative nucleus is shared without derivational lexicalization across Forms I, IV, VIII, the VIII active participle, and the noun balaa'; its distinctive Quran-internal signature is a bi-instrument ('test WITH X') paired with a revealing purpose clause ('to make manifest WHICH/WHETHER Y').
blw.plain_explanation: Across nearly every occurrence, God (or, at the mundane level, a human, or even a soul over its own deeds) puts someone or something through an imposed, decisive experience whose function is to bring a latent quality to light. The instrument is polarity-neutral: it can be hardship (fear, hunger, loss, restriction) OR good (honor, provision, a 'good balaa''), so the root does not mean 'afflict' or 'punish'. The purpose is repeatedly spelled out as discrimination or disclosure — 'which of you is best in deed', 'grateful or ungrateful', 'that God may know who fears Him', 'until We know the strivers', laying bare what is in the breasts and the secrets. A single occurrence (20:120, 'a dominion that does not yablaa') stands apart: it is intransitive, has an inanimate subject, and means 'wear out / decay', with no probative content and no Quran-internal bridge to the trial sense.
blw.strongest_counterexample: 20:120:13:1 (wa-mulkin laa yablaa) is intransitive with an inanimate subject (mulk, dominion), carries no agent, no bi-instrument, and no revealing purpose clause; it means 'wear out / decay / perish' (paired with shajarati l-khuld, the tree of eternity) and its stem-vowel form (yablaa, alif-maqsura, reflecting بلي) differs from the transitive test-verb (yabluu). No Quranic occurrence links this decay sense to the trial sense by shared instrument, subject-type, syntax, or gloss; the lexicographers' 'testing = wearing a thing out' bridge is an external etymological claim and is disallowed under the Quran-internal source policy. It therefore resists unification as a distinct, unbridged intransitive sub-class.
blw.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each reached REPRESENTATIVE/MODERATE with 20:120:13:1 as the sole unbridged resistant occurrence; the aggregator re-confirmed all 38 word_refs, forms, and verse_texts directly against the packet, including the yablaa vs. yabluu stem-vowel distinction and the balaa'-hasan positive pole.

nkr.candidate_root_contribution: nkr contributes the negative pole of recognition/acknowledgment: to place or find something OUTSIDE the domain of the recognized/owned. It runs as one graded derivational family — (a) perceptual failure-to-recognize, X is unfamiliar/strange (nakira 11:70; munkirun 12:58; munkarun 'strangers' 15:62, 51:25; causative nakkiru 'render unrecognizable' 27:41); (b) volitional withholding-of-acknowledgment of the KNOWN, i.e. disavow/repudiate/deny (yunkiru/tunkirun 13:36, 16:83, 40:81; munkirun/munkira 21:50, 23:69, 16:22); and (c) the nominalized 'that which is (rightly) not acknowledged' = al-munkar, the reprehensible/disavowed (the al-maʿruf/al-munkar frame). It is welded Quran-internally by direct ع ر ف (ʿrf) antonymy in the same clause/verse (16:83 yaʿrifuna...thumma yunkirunaha; 12:58 faʿarafahum wa-hum lahu munkirun; 23:69; 22:72 taʿrifu...al-munkar) and by al-maʿruf (itself the ʿrf passive participle) standing opposite al-munkar. It does NOT by itself encode severity, direness, or sensory repugnance.
nkr.plain_explanation: The root's demonstrated centre is 'not-recognizing / refusing-to-acknowledge', the exact opposite of ʿrf ('to recognize'). The Quran stages the two together in single verses: they recognize God's favour, then disavow it (16:83); Joseph recognized his brothers while they did not recognize him (12:58); you recognize the munkar on the deniers' faces (22:72). From this one negative-recognition idea come the strangers who are 'not recognized' (15:62, 51:25), the disguised throne 'made unrecognizable' (27:41), the deniers of the signs (40:81), and, nominalized, al-munkar = 'the not-acknowledged-as-good' = the reprehensible (the standing maʿruf/munkar pairing). One class does NOT reduce to this: the adjective nukr/nukur and the elative ankar mean 'dreadful/dire/harsh/repugnant' (a dire punishment 18:87, 65:8; a dreadful thing 54:6; the donkey's bray as the most jarring of sounds 31:19) — an evaluative sense that pushes away from recognition.
nkr.strongest_counterexample: 31:19 (inna ankara l-aswati la-sawtu l-hamir, 'the most nkr of sounds is the braying of donkeys') does not merely lack recognition-support — it CONTRADICTS a non-recognition nucleus: a donkey's bray is maximally familiar/recognized, yet it is graded the MOST nkr, because the operative sense is 'disagreeable/harsh/repugnant', a value orthogonal to recognition. Reinforcing: in 65:8 nukr stands in internal parallel with an intensity adjective (hisaban shadidan ... adhaban nukran), glossing nukr toward severity, not non-recognition; and 18:87 / 54:6 apply nukr to a real, decreed punishment and to the Reckoning — things that are not 'unrecognized' but 'dire/dreadful'. This evaluative ADJ/elative class is a coherent, internally-supported resistant sub-class and is the ceiling-capping evidence.
nkr.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversarial C) converged on one recognition-negation nucleus plus the same resistant evaluative sub-class; C's strongest counterexample (31:19) and severity parallel (65:8) are adopted as the ceiling-capping evidence.

qTE.candidate_root_contribution: qTE introduces a discontinuity into something continuous, whole, or connected: it severs a part from a whole, breaches a connection, or terminates an ongoing continuity. The continuum is domain-neutral (material, spatial, temporal, relational); the derivation modulates telicity/plurality/voice (I = single telic severance, II = intensive/distributive severance or division into many parts, V = mediopassive coming-apart, N = the piece produced / the severed state / the one who brings to a decisive close).
qTE.plain_explanation: Across 36 occurrences qTE is the operation of cutting: making a break in what was continuous or joined. It appears as a literal severing of bodies and objects (aorta 69:46, thieves' hands 5:38, felled palm-trees 59:5, torn intestines 47:15), as the eradication idiom of cutting off the 'dabir' trailing remnant (6:45, 7:72, 8:7), as severing relational bonds (explicitly the antonym of 'to be joined' at 2:27 and 13:25, kinship at 47:22, the 'asbab' means at 2:166/22:15, communal unity into sects at 21:93/23:53, hearts at 9:110), as nominal 'portions/pieces' of a continuum (a stretch of night 11:81/15:65, patches of dark night 10:27, adjacent land-plots 13:4) and division into organized units (twelve tribes 7:160, nations 7:168), and as the termination/closure of an ongoing state (unending fruit 'not cut off' 56:33, concluding a matter 27:32). One occurrence resists: 9:121 'traverse a valley' means crossing undivided terrain, not severance.
qTE.strongest_counterexample: 9:121:8:1 وَلَا يَقْطَعُونَ وَادِيًا means to traverse/cover a valley (movement through undivided terrain), a sense no other packet occurrence licenses; it resists the severance/discontinuity nucleus on strict Quran-internal evidence. The context (recording of expenditure and ground covered in God's cause) forces 'cross/cover distance', which leaves the valley whole and continuous - the opposite of separation, division, or cessation. Its own root-mate 29:29 تَقْطَعُونَ ٱلسَّبِيلَ (obstruct/sever safe passage) points the opposite pragmatic direction on a near-identical path-object, so the internal path-pair itself refuses to disambiguate toward unity; folding 9:121 in requires a motion-as-line metaphor supplied from outside the corpus, barred under QURAN-INTERNAL ONLY.
qTE.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) converged on the same nucleus, the same single resistant occurrence (9:121), and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade; adversary C's UNRESOLVED sub-verdict is honored by holding 9:121 outside the unified claim.

fwh.candidate_root_contribution: The root ف و ه denotes the mouth — the concrete external oral aperture of the face, the boundary-organ between interior (heart/belly) and exterior through which intake passes in (water: 13:14), emission of speech/breath/manifested states passes out (18:5, 3:118, 61:8/9:32), and which can be physically sealed (36:65). It is a neutral, purely nominal body-part noun; it carries no lexical charge of speech-content, truth, falsity, insincerity, or externality-as-such.
fwh.plain_explanation: Every occurrence of fwh means the physical mouth. Sometimes it is a plain body part (water reaching the mouth in 13:14; hands to mouths in 14:9; mouths sealed in 36:65), and very often it is the aperture from or with which speech issues (words come 'out of' mouths in 18:5; people say things 'with their mouths' in 3:167, 5:41, 9:8, 24:15, 33:4, 9:30; they try to blow out God's light 'with their mouths' in 61:8, 9:32). The frequent hypocrisy/insincerity flavor is not in the word fwh itself: it is built every time by an explicit contrast term — heart (qalb), breast (sadr), knowledge (ilm), or God's truth (haqq). Strip that contrast and the mouth reverts to a neutral organ, as the drinking and gesture verses prove.
fwh.strongest_counterexample: 61:8:5:2 and 9:32:6:2 «يُرِيدُونَ … يُطْفِـُٔوا۟ نُورَ ٱللَّهِ بِأَفْوَٰهِهِمْ» ('to extinguish God's light with their mouths'): 'mouths' is metonymic for breath/propaganda — you do not literally blow out light with a mouth — which could be read as drifting toward a non-organ 'utterance/breath' sense. It does not break the account: the trope depends on the literal image of feeble breath issuing from the mouth-aperture, so it exploits the organ rather than abandoning it; it confirms the aperture-of-emission nucleus and forces no second sense.
fwh.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each concluded the concrete 'mouth' nucleus is over-determined and could not be disproven; all three refuted the enriched-speech reading using the same non-verbal anchors.

njm.candidate_root_contribution: njm names a discrete luminous celestial body — a 'star' — as a class distinct from and enumerated after the sun (shams) and the moon (qamar); a countable point-light (conceived predominantly in multiplicity), holding a determinate position, shining/guiding through darkness, subject to divine command, and impermanent (setting, falling, and finally effaced).
njm.plain_explanation: Across all 13 occurrences the root surfaces only as a noun (no verb, no participle), inflected for number: plural nujūm (9x) and singular najm (4x). Both number-forms refer to the same thing — stars — and bridge cleanly (guidance najm 16:16 mirrors nujūm 6:97; setting najm 53:1 mirrors idbār al-nujūm 52:49; piercing najm 86:3). The Quran repeatedly lists the stars as a third, separate item AFTER sun and moon (16:12, 7:54, 22:18), fixing the referent as the lesser celestial lights rather than sun or moon. Attached features are stable: made for navigation in darkness (6:97, 16:16), possessing positions/settings (56:75, 52:49), objects of observation (37:88), subjected by command and prostrating (16:12, 7:54, 22:18), and eschatologically extinguished (77:8, 81:2). One token — 55:6 (najm paired with shajar/trees, both prostrating) — does not internally force the celestial reading and is the sole residual seam; the packet's own 22:18 (stars and trees co-prostrating) supplies a celestial precedent, but the singular minimal couplet of 55:6 remains underdetermined on Quran-internal evidence alone.
njm.strongest_counterexample: 55:6 wa-al-najmu wa-al-shajaru yasjudāni: singular najm is bound in a tight two-member couplet with shajar (trees), and the immediately preceding 55:5 (al-shamsu wa-al-qamaru bi-ḥusbān) already closes the celestial pair — structurally inviting najm here to be a low/stemless ground-vegetation term paired against woody trees. Quran-internal evidence cannot decisively exclude this terrestrial-flora reading, since no other token forces the celestial sense of THIS word and the immediate collocation is botanical; this leaves a possible unbridged non-celestial sub-reading on one token, which caps the account at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE.
njm.independent_verification: Cross-analyst: A and C independently grade MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE citing 55:6 resistance and single-form (N-only) morphology; B grades STRONG only under strict external-lexicon exclusion and concedes MODERATE if any botanical prior is admitted. The convergent honest floor is MODERATE with 55:6 as the residual crack.

xll.plain_explanation: The root خ ل ل surfaces in the Quran only as nominals (13/13 tagged N; no verb anywhere), and these fall into two groups the text never links. One group, spatial khilāl (خِلَٰل / خِلَٰلَ / خِلَٰلِ + suffix), means the interior gaps/interstices distributed through a single many-parted whole — a garden, twin gardens, the earth, a heaped/spread cloud, a cluster of dwellings, a human throng — through which water flows or people move (17:5, 9:47, 17:91, 18:33, 27:61, 24:43, 30:48). The other group, relational khalīl / khullah / akhillāʾ, means an intimate one deliberately takes as a friend, a bond that is fragile and turns to enmity at Judgment unless grounded in taqwā (4:125, 17:73, 25:28, 43:67, 2:254, and 14:31). The single word خِلَٰلٌ in 14:31 has the very shape of the spatial word yet means befriending, fixed by the near-identical Day-frame in 2:254 (خُلَّةٌ). Because no verse ever joins the spatial and relational senses, and the sole crossover form is a homograph, the Quran-internal evidence does not license one shared nucleus. Each class is clean on its own; their unity is unresolved (leaning homonymy).
xll.strongest_counterexample: 14:31 خِلَٰلٌ shares the exact surface skeleton of spatial khilāl (17:5 خِلَٰلَ / 24:43 خِلَٰلِهِ) yet is fixed as 'befriending' by the near-verbatim Day-frame parallel 'yawmun laa bayʿun fiihi wa-laa ___' in 2:254 (خُلَّةٌ), so the same form carries a relational sense with zero interstitial content — blocking any single Quran-internal nucleus.
xll.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) converged on two unbridged classes with 14:31 as the resistant seam; A and B proposed MODERATE two-class, C proposed RESISTANT/UNRESOLVED for the unified claim — aggregated to UNRESOLVED per the no-bridge coherence rule.

$yE.candidate_root_contribution: A bounded body of people individuated within a larger whole by shared alignment/course/kind — a side, party, or faction, characteristically a proper part set off against other such bodies (and against the enemy). Valence is contextual, not lexical: it spans commended solidarity (Abraham of Noah's party 37:83; Moses' side 28:15) and condemned fragmentation (the sects produced by dividing religion 6:159, 30:32; imposed factionalism 28:4, 6:65). It does not entail kinship, contemporaneity, a living leader, or fixed polarity. The lone verbal token (24:19, indecency 'spreading/becoming current') is retained inside the same derivational family but is a semi-detached, singly-attested dynamic sense not independently bridged to the nominal nucleus Quran-internally.
$yE.plain_explanation: For 11 of 12 occurrences, ش ي ع names a distinguishable grouping of people held together by a common allegiance, course, or kind, and marked off from others — 'one's side/party' (شِيعَة), 'factions/sects' (شِيَعًا), or 'counterparts of the same kind' (أَشْيَاع). The word itself carries no fixed praise or blame; the surrounding context (siding with Moses vs. being made to fight; Abraham's righteous camp vs. religion split into rival sects) supplies the valence. One verb (تَشِيعَ, 24:19) means an abstract thing 'spreading' through people and denotes no group at all; it is kept in the same family but is the single case the nominal account cannot govern.
$yE.strongest_counterexample: 24:19:5:1 «أَن تَشِيعَ الْفَـحِشَةُ فِى الَّذِين ءَامَنُوا» — the lone verb. Its subject is an abstract act (الفَاحِشَة), not people; the sense is purely 'spread / become current' with zero grouping, party, or allegiance content. It resists any account built on 'faction/following' and can be salvaged only by retreating to an over-abstract 'coursing/propagation' nucleus resting on this single attestation — reasoning from morphology-family to sense, which the contract warns is not identity. Quran-internally the verb and the eleven nouns share no co-text, syntactic frame, or derivational demonstration (only a thin فِى-collective frame parallel), so the bridge is not independently established. This is the principal ceiling on confidence.
$yE.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (bottom-up A, derivational-distinctiveness B, adversarial C) converged on the same nominal nucleus, the same single resistant verbal token, and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE ceiling.

TmE.candidate_root_contribution: TmE encodes an active, forward-leaning eager desire directed at an unattained future good — an expectant reaching-toward whose object is desired but not yet possessed and typically not within the subject's own power. It is the appetitive/positive pole set explicitly against the aversive pole of خَوْف (reaching vs. recoil). The lexeme is valence-neutral: whether an instance reads as legitimate hope, naive expectation, or culpable covetousness/presumption is supplied entirely by context (the object's licitness and whether the aspirant has warrant), never by the root itself.
TmE.plain_explanation: Across all 12 occurrences طمع names an eager reaching toward something wanted but not yet had. In the fixed pair خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا (lightning shown, or God invoked, in fear-and-طمع) it is the hopeful counterpart of fear. As a verb it almost always governs أَنْ + a not-yet-realized favorable outcome (being forgiven, admitted to the Garden, increased, others believing). The very same construction is praised for the deserving (Ibrahim, believers at 5:84) and rebuked for the presumptuous (70:38, 74:15) or the predatory (33:32) — so the moral color is contextual, not built into the word.
TmE.strongest_counterexample: 33:32 فَيَطْمَعَ ٱلَّذِى فِى قَلْبِهِۦ مَرَضٌ — the only verbal token that is simultaneously illicit/predatory, absolute (no أَنْ-complement), and directed at a person rather than a divine/eschatological outcome. It most pressures any pure 'hope' gloss. It nonetheless bridges to the one nucleus: soft speech (a perceptual cue of attainability) kindles eager reaching toward a not-possessed object, exactly parallel to lightning kindling طمع for rain in 13:12/30:24; its أَنْ-less syntax is shared with the licit 7:46, so the absolute construction spans both valences and marks no separate sense. Its negativity is supplied by the illicit object and diseased subject, not by a distinct lexeme.
TmE.independent_verification: All three independent lenses (A, B, C) ran the two-sense disproof and independently found it collapses on the 5:84↔70:38 minimal pair, and all three independently judged 33:32 to bridge rather than resist.

Tfq.candidate_root_contribution: ط ف ق realizes a single frozen, defective inceptive/ingressive verb — 'set about / began (to do)' — that contributes aspectual onset-plus-engagement only, while the lexical content of the action is borne entirely by an obligatory following complement (a finite imperfect verb يخصفان, or an accusative maṣdar مسحًا). It denotes no concrete act, no completion/result, no moral valence, and no argument structure of its own.
Tfq.plain_explanation: Across all three Quranic occurrences the root appears only as a perfect verb (طَفِقَا / طَفِقَ) that means the subject 'took up / set about' doing something. طفق itself never names the activity — the activity is supplied by whatever follows it: 'they set about STITCHING leaves over themselves' (7:22, 20:121) and 'he set about WIPING the legs and necks' (38:33). Because the very same طفق attaches to two different kinds of complement (a finite verb and a bare verbal noun) yet the constant contributed sense is only 'commenced/undertook,' its own content is aspectual (phase-onset), not lexical. The account is internally clean but rests on thin evidence: three tokens, of which 7:22 and 20:121 are a near-verbatim echo of one Adam episode, leaving effectively two independent contexts and only one verbal form (perfect).
Tfq.strongest_counterexample: 38:33 (فَطَفِقَ مَسْحًۢا بِٱلسُّوقِ وَٱلْأَعْنَاقِ) is the sole adversarial boundary: it is the only context outside the Adam/Eve narrative — i.e. the only genuinely independent data point — and it breaks the canonical 'طفق + finite imperfect' template by taking an accusative maṣdar complement (مسحًا) instead of a finite verb (contrast يخصفان). This changed construction keeps a live competing 'thin lexical verb' reading ('he applied himself to a wiping') available, so the class is not adversarially clean at the syntactic level. It does NOT, however, semantically break the account: 'he set about wiping' fits comfortably, so 38:33 caps strength and scope but does not overturn the inceptive nucleus.
Tfq.independent_verification: Adversary C independently affirmed the nucleus while challenging breadth; effective independent contexts number ~2, insufficient to certify distinctiveness.

dEE.candidate_root_contribution: Forceful, violent thrusting / shoving / driving of a person. The geminate root د-ع-ع supplies harsh, propulsive MANNER applied to a human patient; DIRECTION (away, as in repelling the orphan; toward a goal, as in driving to the Fire) is not encoded by the root but is supplied by argument structure (bare accusative object vs. إِلَىٰ + goal). The intensive register is corroborated by the cognate accusative دَعًّا.
dEE.plain_explanation: In its 3 Quranic occurrences (2 verses, effectively 2 independent contexts) the root د-ع-ع describes forcefully shoving or driving a person. In 107:2 the denier of the dīn physically thrusts/rebuffs the orphan (يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ, bare object). In 52:13 the deniers are violently driven toward the Fire (يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا, passive + intensifying verbal noun). The common core is a harsh, violent propulsion of a human being; whether the person is pushed away or driven toward something is fixed by the sentence, not by the root.
dEE.strongest_counterexample: The directional split is the sharpest datum: 107:2:3:1 يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ has a bare accusative and thrusts the patient OFF/away, while 52:13:2:1 يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ drives the patients TOWARD an explicit goal. These mutually refute any single directional gloss: 'drive toward' is disproven by 107:2, 'repel away' is disproven by 52:13's إِلَىٰ. The account survives only by retreating to a direction-neutral 'forceful thrust of a person', which is broad; and it caps confidence because the unity is bought at the cost of specificity.
dEE.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each attempted the strongest counterexamples (directional split; 107:2 socio-moral reading) and each concluded the core holds while flagging the same breadth/distinctiveness limits; convergence is recorded but does not substitute for an untested neighbour-root distinctiveness check.

ftr.candidate_root_contribution: ftr marks the flagging / abatement / lapse that breaks a sustained continuity or maximal intensity — a relaxation OUT OF an already-running, uninterrupted state. It is realized derivationally across three forms of one root: Form I intransitive (the agent's own effort flags — 21:20 لَا يَفْتُرُونَ), Form II causative-passive (an intensity is made to ease off a patient — 43:75 لَا يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ), and the verbal noun (the reified interval of such lapse in a continuous series — 5:19 فَتْرَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ). The nucleus presupposes prior sustainedness and names its diminution, not its onset, content, or final termination.
ftr.plain_explanation: Across its three Quranic occurrences the root ف ت ر consistently names a let-up in something that is (or should be) kept going without break.
