The angels 'do not yaftur' — they never slacken in ceaseless glorification (21:20). The punishment of hell 'is not yufattaru off them' — it is never made to ease or abate (43:75). And a messenger comes 'ʿalā fatratin' — during a gap/lull in the succession of messengers (5:19). Two of the three are under negation, so the positive sense (slackening) is asserted by what the negation denies; the noun is the one non-negated, realized instance of an actual lapse. The three sit in three unrelated domains (worship, torment, prophetic history) yet converge on one abstraction, which argues for a genuine unified nucleus rather than context-borrowing.
ftr.strongest_counterexample: 5:19 فَتْرَةٍ (N) is the category-shifter and the chief limiter on the grade: the two verbs denote a dynamic event (flagging / being abated) while the noun denotes a reified span of time ('a fatra of the messengers', partitive مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ). Reading it into the verbal nucleus requires the inferential step 'the interval IS the period during which the sending slackened' — a step no verse in the packet licenses, since there is no second nominal token to confirm it. The verse reads coherently on a flat temporal-sequence gap ('an interval between messengers') with the 'slackening' connotation supplied only externally. This is a candidate lexicalized/nominal sub-class, and per contract a nominal lexicalization risk caps strength at MODERATE and scope at REPRESENTATIVE. (Resistance is mild rather than material: the verse's own logic — the pleadable excuse مَا جَآءَنَا مِن بَشِيرٍ وَلَا نَذِيرٍ presupposes a real break in continuity — keeps the noun inside the nucleus, which is why the class is flagged as an adversarial boundary, not a final-RESISTANT seam.)
ftr.independent_verification: All three lenses (A, B, C) independently reached MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE and independently identified 5:19 فَتْرَة as the single lexicalization-risk / category-shift limiter; no lens found a materially failing occurrence.

jAr.candidate_root_contribution: To raise an urgent, overt (audible) outcry wrung out by acute affliction, functioning as an appeal for relief/rescue. The distress-trigger and appeal-function are the recurrent nucleus; the addressee (God) and the outcome (heard vs. refused) are supplied by context, not by the root.
jAr.plain_explanation: Every attested token of this root (all Form I imperfect, masculine plural: تَجْـَٔرُونَ / يَجْـَٔرُونَ / لَا تَجْـَٔرُوا) describes people crying out under duress. In 16:53 the cry is triggered by harm (ٱلضُّرُّ) and directed 'to Him' (فَإِلَيْهِ). In 23:64 the punished affluent ones (مُتْرَفِيهِم) cry out the instant the punishment (ٱلْعَذَاب) seizes them, with no stated addressee. In 23:65 that same cry is forbidden and declared futile — 'do not cry out today; you will not be helped (لَا تُنصَرُونَ)' — which retro-construes the outcry as a plea for rescue. So the root names the affliction-driven outcry-for-relief itself, morally neutral, not a formulated prayer, not a guarantee of being answered, and not inherently addressed to God.
jAr.strongest_counterexample: 23:64 (يَجْـَٔرُونَ) is bare — no addressee and no explicit appeal — so read in isolation it could denote a mere wordless scream of anguish, undercutting the 'appeal for relief' component and favoring a thinner acoustic-only nucleus. It is neutralized by its own continuation 23:65 ('do not cry out today; you will not be helped'), which construes that very cry as a plea for rescue; it therefore caps the pragmatic 'appeal' layer as context-reinforced rather than breaking the affliction-outcry nucleus.
jAr.independent_verification: All three independent lenses (A, B, C) concur: one root nucleus, no resistant sub-class, appeal-vs-acoustic sub-question unresolved, grade MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE.

kwr.candidate_root_contribution: In Form II (the only attested form), kwr applies a winding / coiling / wrapping-over motion: one thing is wound or laid over/around another in an enveloping, circling overlay. This is Quran-internally demonstrable for the 39:5 class, where the frame X عَلَى Y (accusative object + عَلَى + locus) runs reciprocally in BOTH directions (night wound over day AND day wound over night); the reversibility of the identical action fixes a symmetric mutual-overlay nucleus, not a one-way covering. The same verse fences kwr off from create (خَلَقَ), harness/subdue (سَخَّرَ), and course/run (يَجْرِى). The nucleus is scoped as REPRESENTATIVE, not universal, because the single passive terminal token (81:1) does not Quran-internally license the winding content and is carried only by inference.
kwr.plain_explanation: The root shows up only as a Form II verb, three times, in just two verse-settings. In 39:5 God 'winds' the night over the day and the day over the night — the very same act done both ways, which tells us kwr is about wrapping/overlaying one thing over another, and the verse itself keeps it distinct from creating, harnessing, and making-run. In 81:1 'when the sun is kuwwirat', the sun is acted on alone, passively, at the end of the world; here the text gives us only 'something terminal happens to the sun' — the specific 'wound-up/rolled-up' reading is a plausible extension of 39:5 but is not proven from the Quranic wording, so that token is held as an unresolved seam rather than forced into the nucleus.
kwr.strongest_counterexample: 81:1:3:1 كُوِّرَتْ ('when the sun is kuwwirat') is the resisting occurrence. It strips away every feature that fixes the 39:5 nucleus: it is the only passive, the only single-argument (sole patient, no accusative object), the only perfective, and the only token lacking a عَلَى-locus and a reciprocal partner. It does not contradict the winding account so much as fail to license it: Quran-internally only 'a terminal passive event befalls the sun' is recoverable, and projecting 'winding/rolling-up' onto it is an inference (drawn from 39:5 and the surrounding eschatological verbs), not a demonstration from the token itself.
kwr.independent_verification: Cross-lens: Lens A and Lens C independently identify 81:1:3:1 as the resisting/underdetermined token; Lens B's assimilation is the minority position and is downgraded to PLAUSIBLE, not established.

Eml.candidate_root_contribution: ع م ل denotes agentive, effort-bearing enactment or production attributable to a doer: the carried-out act, the sustained practice, or the fashioned output that issues from an agent's exercised capacity and is thereafter imputed back to that agent. The finite verb (Form I only), the maSdar/plural عمل~أعمال (the act/product as a storable, weighable record), and the participle عامل (the agent) are one nucleus. The root is morally neutral in itself; righteous or evil valence is supplied only by an added qualifier, object, or the recompense frame, never by the root.
Eml.plain_explanation: ع م ل is 'to do/make/work' in the sense of an agent actually carrying something out, so that the result is credited to that agent. What is done ranges from a physical artifact (armor, statues, cattle) to bare toil to moral conduct. The noun names the deed or product as a record that can be paid, weighed, or nullified; the participle names the worker. Goodness or evil is added by context, not carried by the root itself. The overwhelmingly common 'righteous deeds / God sees what you do / deeds made vain' usage is a dominant deployment of this neutral core, not the core's own meaning.
Eml.strongest_counterexample: 36:71:7:1 مِّمَّا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِينَآ أَنْعَٰمًا — God's hands 'made' cattle. It defeats the salient moral-deed reading on three axes: the agent is God (no accountability/recompense), the product is a living creature (not a deed), and عمل stands in apposition to خَلَقْنَا; this forces the neutral, productive width of the nucleus and shows the moral-conduct sense is a contextual specialization, not the root floor.
Eml.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, C) each opened the full 360-occurrence packet; A and C independently graded MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE and B graded STRONG/COMPREHENSIVE, with the divergence resolved against B because the manufacture/labour uses (34:11, 34:13, 36:71, 9:60, 18:79) form a coherent resistant sub-class to the distinctive moral-deed account and 11:46 materially resists.

kbr.candidate_root_contribution: kbr marks that something ranks HIGH / EXCEEDS on an open magnitude scale (the positive pole opposite s-gh-r 'smallness'), the dimension being context-supplied: physical size, quantity, accumulated years, social rank/seniority, moral gravity, weight-of-burden, or degree/importance. The root is scalar and comparative-productive (akbar min) and morally NEUTRAL; direction (self vs other), valence (praise vs blame), and the 'refuse-to-submit' surplus are contributed by morphology and context, not by the root.
kbr.plain_explanation: The root kbr means 'great / exceeding on a scale of magnitude.' It is the opposite pole of 'small' (the recurrent saghir/kabir and asghar/akbar pairings), and it is neutral: it equally modifies great reward and great sin, God's grandeur and Pharaoh's coveted supremacy. Every derived stem is a regular operation on this one scalar idea: form II 'declare [God] great' (magnify), form IV 'deem another great' (awe, 12:31), and the large forms V/X family 'make/claim oneself great' (self-magnification). The self-magnification family is blameworthy in creatures precisely because it is claimed 'without right' (bi-ghayri l-haqq), while the identical participle names God in praise (al-Mutakabbir, 59:23) and God's kibriya' is rightful (45:37). This is one nucleus with a morphologically transparent derivational family, not two roots.
kbr.strongest_counterexample: The identical form-V participle carries incompatible settled senses purely by referent: al-Mutakabbir (59:23:15:2) is a praiseworthy divine name, while al-mutakabbirin (40:76) names Hell's inmates and 'an tatakabbara fiha' (7:13:8:1) is rebellious self-exaltation. Likewise 'aba wa-stakbara' (2:34:10:2) carries the surplus 'refused a rightful command' that bare 'was big' cannot generate, and 'kabura ala l-mushrikin' (42:13:24:1) means 'is grievous/intolerable to them,' straining a pure size reading. These show the derived-stem senses are lexicalized with surplus and referent-dependent valence, capping the unity claim below STRONG.
kbr.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A base-up morphology, B nucleus-vs-family, C adversary) each read all 161 occurrences and independently converged on one scalar-magnitude nucleus with a transparent derivational family graded MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE, with the same residual lexicalized sub-classes flagged.

gyr.candidate_root_contribution: Relational NON-IDENTITY: gyr marks a referent as other-than / distinct-from a specified standard X. It is inherently two-place and functional, carrying no positive descriptive content of its own — it only brackets what falls outside the identity of X. In the derived stems this same 'otherness' is verbalized: Form II (causative) = make-other = alter; Form V (mediopassive) = become-other = change.
gyr.plain_explanation: In ~95% of its occurrences gyr is the single case-inflected word ghayr, a relational operator meaning 'other than / not-the-same-as' a named foil: 'no god other than Him', 'people other than you', 'a reward not-cut-off', 'without knowledge/right/reckoning'. It brackets good, bad and neutral alike, so it has no built-in evaluation, and it names a static difference, not a process. The six derived-stem verbs (Forms II and V) add the event: to make something other (alter) or to become other (change) — e.g. 'God does not change what is in a people until they change what is in themselves', 'milk whose taste does not become-other'. The Quran itself glosses change as producing ghayr ('the earth is changed into other-than-the-earth', 14:48; 'skins other than theirs', 4:56), which bridges the noun and the verbs. One occurrence, 100:3 al-mughirat ('the raiders/chargers at dawn', a Form-IV hapax in a martial oath series), has no Quran-internal path to otherness and is left resistant.
gyr.strongest_counterexample: 100:3:1:3 fa-al-mughirat subhan ('the chargers/raiders at dawn'), a Form-IV hapax and the sole N(IV) in the root, embedded in a martial oath series (al-'adiyat / al-muriyat / al-mughirat) whose members denote violent cavalry motion. On no Quran-internal evidence does 'the raiders at dawn' reduce to otherness, difference, or change; the only route to fold it in ('a raid makes things other') requires the external lexical premise that aghara 'to raid' shares the gyr nucleus, which the source policy forbids. It is therefore an unbridged, lexicalized/homonymous nominal that no single account covers, and it caps the whole-root claim below STRONG/UNIVERSAL.
gyr.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, and adversary C) converged on the same nucleus, the same 153/154 coverage, and the same single resistant occurrence 100:3.

nEm.candidate_root_contribution: A pleasant, benefit-bearing condition of well-being/ease - being in it, being put into it, or the good thing that constitutes it: the positive well-being pole opposed to harm/adversity (Darra'/shar/kufr), prototypically bestowed (default giver = Allah) and calling for grateful acknowledgment. It is realized relationally as a conferred favor (niEmah / >anEama), experientially as enjoyed bliss or worldly ease (naEiym / naEmah / naAEimah / naE~ama), and grammaticalized as a laudative evaluation 'how excellent / how good is X' (jamid niEma). This nucleus governs the derivational family (~107 occ.); it does NOT extend to the lexicalized concrete count-noun >anEam/naEam 'grazing livestock' (~33 occ.), whose link to 'benefit' is carried by neighbouring words, is undemonstrated Quran-internally, and is even inverted in pejorative similes.
nEm.plain_explanation: Across most of its occurrences the root n-E-m names good, pleasant well-being: a favor granted (niEmah), the act of granting it (>anEama), the enjoyed bliss of the Garden (naEiym), worldly ease/soft-living (naEmah, naE~ama, naAEimah), and a frozen verb of praise ('excellent is...'). All of these hang together as one field of 'agreeable good, bestowed / enjoyed / declared,' the opposite of harm and ingratitude. But the same consonants also spell a completely concrete word, >anEam 'grazing livestock/cattle,' which the Qur'an uses as an ordinary animal term and even as an image of sub-rational heedlessness ('like cattle, nay more astray'). That livestock sense is not the well-being nucleus applied; it is a separate lexicalized noun. So the honest result is one coherent nucleus over a derivational family plus one unbridged concrete class - not a single unified meaning over all 140 tokens.
nEm.strongest_counterexample: 7:179:24:3 'kal->anEam bal hum >aDall' (identically 25:44:11:3; reinforced by 47:12:19:2 'ya'kuluwna kama ta'kulu l->anEam' and Satanic ear-slitting of >anEam at 4:119:6:2). Here the identical consonantal root, which elsewhere names the bliss the righteous are questioned about and the Gardens of naEiym, surfaces as a bare concrete count-noun deployed to DEGRADE humans as sub-rational beasts - the semantic antipode of the well-being nucleus. No verse derives the animal sense from the good-state sense, so their unity would be asserted, not shown; this single datum blocks any STRONG/unified reading and caps the result at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE.
nEm.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) converged on the same nucleus, the same C1-C6 fault-lines, the same cognate-accusative bridges (8:53, 27:19), and the same strongest counterexample (7:179 / 25:44 / 47:12).

nZr.candidate_root_contribution: To direct one's gaze/attention toward a designated object across a gap. In form I this is concretely realized as look-at (naZara ilaa a viewable thing), examine/consider (naZara + kayfa/maadhaa/fii, turning attention on evidence), watch-on/behold (absolute spectator posture), and await an anticipated event (hal/maa yanZuruuna illaa + an impending event); the derived form VIII (intaZara/muntaZir-) lexicalizes this same edge as free-standing await/wait-for. The bridge from perception to expectant regard is attested Quran-internally, not imposed. This account does NOT extend to the form-IV respite family (see resistant class).
nZr.plain_explanation: nZr is about aiming your attention at something, not about the result of seeing it. Depending on what you aim at, that becomes: looking at a present thing, examining evidence to consider how/what, watching a scene unfold, or waiting for something that is coming. Form VIII (intaZara) is just the settled word for wait. A separate branch, form IV (anZara) plus the form-I noun naZira in 2:280, means grant a delay / respite - giving someone time, not looking at them - and the Quran never links that meaning to seeing, so it stands apart.
nZr.strongest_counterexample: 2:280 naZiratun (a deferment until ease) is a form-I nominal meaning respite with zero perceptual or attentional content, aligning with the form-IV respite class rather than the perception/attention nucleus. It is the cleanest internal proof that nZr does not reduce to one meaning even within form I, and it aligns with the whole form-IV respite class, which is materially unbridged to the perception nucleus.
nZr.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B sense-pole, C adversarial) all returned REPRESENTATIVE/MODERATE with the same resistant respite class; convergent but short of an adversarially clean root-wide SUPPORTED result.

jhd.candidate_root_contribution: jhd = the straining of one's capacity/effort to its utmost limit. In the Form-III derivational family (verb jaahada/yujaahidu, participle mujaahid, masdar jihaad) this utmost exertion is realized as DIRECTED and dyadic — brought to bear toward a cause or against a resistant counterpart — but the target, instrument, and moral valence are supplied entirely by the syntactic complement (fii sabiili llaah / fii / bi- / direct object / li-tushrik), never by the root itself. The base nouns jahd/juhd carry only the scalar component (utmost degree / full capacity) with no directedness.
jhd.plain_explanation: The root names bringing effort to its maximum. When it appears in the Form-III pattern (the verb 'jaahada', the doer 'mujaahid', the verbal noun 'jihaad') it means to bring that maximal effort to bear on something — toward a goal or against an opponent — where WHAT the goal is, HOW (by wealth, by self, by the Qur'an), and whether it is good or evil are all fixed by the surrounding words, not by the root. In its plain noun forms jahd/juhd it means only 'the utmost extent' (of an oath) or 'all the capacity one can find', with no fighting and no direction at all.
jhd.strongest_counterexample: 31:15:2:1 (twin 29:8:6:1) — wa-in jaahadaaka Calaa an tushrika bii: the same Form-III verb of the 'strive in God's way' cluster has PARENTS as agents and shirk as the aim. This decisively disproves that jhd (or Form III specifically) lexically encodes righteous/religious striving; valence and target live in the complement, not the root. The strongest RESISTER to any single-nucleus unification is the frozen base-noun idiom jahda aymaanihim (16:38, 24:53, 35:42, 5:53, 6:109) plus juhdahum (9:79): these carry only the scalar 'utmost degree/capacity' and never exhibit the directed exertion-against-resistance of the Form-III family — same gloss, not a Quran-internally demonstrated common operation.
jhd.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) converged on the identical two-layer structure and the identical MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade; C additionally pressure-tested the multi-class alternative and still declined UNIVERSAL/STRONG.

$rb.candidate_root_contribution: ش ر ب contributes the DRINKING relation to a liquid — the oral taking-in of a liquid — realized through a transparent derivational family: the act (Form-I verb, maṣdar شُرْب shurb), the beverage/thing-drunk (شَرَاب sharāb), the agent (شَارِب shārib), the drinking-place/source (مَشْرَب/مَشَارِب mashrab/mashārib), and the apportioned drinking-turn (شِرْب shirb). The root fixes only the drinking relation; the liquid's identity (water, milk, honey, wine, boiling ḥamīm, muhl, pure drink), its quality/valence, and the quantity/manner are all supplied contextually, not by the root.
$rb.plain_explanation: Across 38 of 39 occurrences the root means literally to drink a liquid, or names something built directly on that act (the drink, the drinker, the drinking-place, the drinking-turn, the manner of drinking). The same word شَرَاب labels a paradisal pure drink and boiling torment-water alike, so the root carries no good/bad charge of its own. The one exception is 2:93 (Form IV, وَأُشْرِبُوا۟ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ, 'they were made to imbibe the calf into their hearts'), a figurative saturation of the heart with no liquid and no mouth. That single figurative token, morphologically unique and not triangulable against any second Quranic occurrence, keeps the account short of a universal literal identity and caps the strength.
$rb.strongest_counterexample: 2:93:15:2 وَأُشْرِبُوا۟ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ — the only Form-IV token and the only figurative use: a non-liquid object (the calf/its love) 'made to imbibe' into the hearts, not the mouth. The bridge from oral drinking to interior psychological saturation is attested by this single, morphologically unique datum, with no second figurative شرب to triangulate it Quran-internally, so it cannot be certified as reducible to the literal nucleus and stands as material resistance capping the unified claim.
$rb.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B class-structure, C adversarial) all read 39/39 and converged on the literal nucleus and on 2:93 as the sole resistant/uncertain token; C's adversarial cap was adopted over A/B's STRONG grade.

ftH.candidate_root_contribution: To undo a pre-existing closure: to move something from a shut, withheld, or unresolved state into openness, so that it becomes accessible, released, disclosed, or decisively resolved. The root presupposes (a) a prior state of closure/withholding/undecidedness and (b) an agent (overwhelmingly God) who removes it; it does not create, break, or merely give.
ftH.plain_explanation: Across all 38 occurrences the root ف ت ح contributes one motivated idea: un-closing what was shut. The physical prototype is opening a container or a gate (baggage 12:65; gates of the sky 15:14, 54:11, 78:19; gates of Hell and Paradise 39:71, 39:73). From this the Quran extends the same act along transparent axes: 'to open upon' someone = to release/bestow/disclose what was withheld (mercy 35:2, blessings 7:96, gates of everything as istidraj 6:44, disclosed knowledge 2:76); and 'to open between parties with truth' = to render a decisive verdict resolving a standoff (7:89, 34:26, 26:118). The nominal al-fatH names that decisive outcome/breakthrough (48:1, 110:1, 61:13, the day of decision 32:29), sought via form X istaftaHa (8:19, 2:89, 14:15), and mafatiH is the derived instrument ('keys') of access (6:59, 24:61). The internal anchor is 35:2, where fatH is set explicitly against imsak (withholding) and paired with irsal (release), fixing the nucleus as 'un-withhold / un-close' rather than crude physical 'open'.
ftH.strongest_counterexample: 28:76:14:1 (Qarun): 'inna mafatiHahu latanuu bi-l-Uzbati uli l-quwwati' — the referent is heavy hoarded wealth that weighs down a band of strong men. Read as 'hoards/treasure-stores' the token denotes a mass of goods, not an act of opening, and even 'keys' strains (keys do not weigh down strongmen); the un-closing component is fully bleached. The only route back to the nucleus is a two-step, Quran-undemonstrated metonymy (open -> key -> what the key guards -> treasure); the packet nowhere states that keys open stores. This is a genuine lexicalized concrete nominal that the packet cannot bridge, and it forbids a STRONG/UNIVERSAL verdict.
ftH.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) converged on the same nucleus and independently identified 28:76 as the strongest counterexample and the bayna/al-fattaH frame as the most resistant class; the aggregator confirmed all word_refs, forms, and verse_text against the packet.

sbq.candidate_root_contribution: Relational/positional ADVANCE: to come to occupy a position ahead of a specified reference point along an ordering (time, a physical course, or attainment/rank), so that the reference point is left behind, not-yet-reached, outrun, or foreclosed. The root is inherently comparative — it always presupposes a second point that is behind, later, outpaced, or pre-empted. WHICH ordering (space/time/rank) and WHICH relation (overtake / escape / pre-empt / be-foremost) is supplied by the construction (particle, subject, form), not by the root itself.
sbq.plain_explanation: sbq is about being or getting AHEAD of something on some ordered line. On a course it is to overtake or race past (Joseph's brothers racing, night not outstripping day); toward God as reference it is the (always-failed) attempt to get beyond His reach; with a decree/allotment as subject it is a word or good outcome that already stands ahead of and forecloses a judgment; and as the participle sabiq it is the front-runner, the foremost in faith or good works. One relational idea — position-ahead-of-a-reference — read on three axes (time, space, rank).
sbq.strongest_counterexample: 21:101:3:1 — inna alladhiina sabaqat lahum minnaa al-Husnaa. The grammatical subject of sabaqat is al-Husnaa (the good outcome), which 'preceded FOR them' (benefactive laam). There is no course, no rival, nothing left behind — only 'was already appointed/stands prior.' If the nucleus is fixed at the distinctive, information-rich reading that Class B and 36:40 actually license (outstrip / get ahead of a rival / be un-overtakeable), 21:101 refutes it outright: the good does not 'outstrip' anyone. Unity is preserved only by retreating to bare temporal antecedence, which is precisely the thin end of the account — the concession that caps the grade at MODERATE.
sbq.independent_verification: Two of three independent lenses (A, C) converged on MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE on exactly these grounds; lens B's STRONG/UNIVERSAL was rejected on its own self-identified point of doubt (the lexicalized decree/escape collocations).

qrn.plain_explanation: The root ق ر ن (qrn) has 36 Quran-internal occurrences that fall into classes with no demonstrable Quran-internal bridge. (1) The largest class (20 base-noun occurrences, qarn/qurun singular and plural) denotes a bygone people/era-cohort: it is overwhelmingly the object of ahlakna 'We destroyed' and ansha'na 'We produced-after', framed by succession and pastness (min qablikum, al-ula, ansha'na min ba'dihim ... akharin) and characterized by human predicates (better in possessions 19:74, mightier in force 50:36/28:78, walking in their dwellings 20:128/32:26). Nothing in these 20 activates 'joining/coupling'. (2) A separate derivational family (8 fa'il associate-nouns qarin/qurana' plus 5 II/IV/VIII participles muqarran/muqrin/muqtarin) coheres around CONJUNCTION: coupling/binding entities into a pair or file (muqarranin fi al-asfad 14:49/38:38, the imposed devil-consort qarin 43:36/4:38, angels coming-alongside muqtarinin 43:53, capacity-to-yoke muqrinin 43:13). (3) A dual-of-qarn epithet (dhu al-qarnayn, 3 occurrences) is given no internal predication of what the two qarn are and is opaque. The etymological bridge 'a generation = people conjoined in one age' is a lexicographer's inference the Quran never surfaces; the source policy forbids treating it as authority. Per 'same root != one meaning' and the mandate to prefer the narrowest account and choose UNRESOLVED when senses have no Quran-internal bridge, the honest root-level result is multiple unbridged classes, not one nucleus. Sub-class accounts are recorded (coupling family; era-cohort class) but neither is promoted to a root claim.
qrn.strongest_counterexample: 46:17:11:2 — wa-qad khalati al-qurunu min qabli ('the qurun have passed away before me'): the operative sense is purely temporal predecessor-peoples; the conjunction/coupling feature is wholly inert, so a coupling-based unifier is not the operative sense here without importing an inference the text never makes. Reinforced by 50:36 (a mightier, destroyed people of a bygone age) and by 18:83 (dhu al-qarnayn), where the dual of the very same base noun yields an opaque proper epithet with no internal gloss — disproof of unity from inside one stem.
qrn.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, and adversary C) each independently partitioned the 36 into the same era-cohort / conjunction-family / opaque-dual structure and each concluded no Quran-internal bridge exists; convergent multi-class verdict.

glZ.candidate_root_contribution: غ ل ظ marks the DENSE / THICK / STOUT pole — being substantial and firm, and hence resistant to softening, yielding, or breaking. It is the antithesis of soft/thin/pliant. The concrete anchor is 48:29 (فَٱسْتَغْلَظَ), a crop-shoot thickening into a stout stalk; the same non-softness is projected onto disposition (hard heart 3:159, stern angels 66:6, commanded sternness 9:73/66:9, ghilẓa in combat 9:123). The root does NOT itself carry moral valence — context supplies it (commanded, angelic and covenantal uses are approved; hard-heartedness is disapproved). It is distinct from shidād (power/might, co-occurs at 66:6), from fazz (coarse manner, distinguished at 3:159), and from ʿaẓīm (magnitude, used separately at 48:29).
glZ.plain_explanation: At root, غ ل ظ means being thick, dense and firm rather than thin, slight or soft. The only literal use (a plant stem growing stout, 48:29) fixes this concrete core, and 3:159 confirms it from inside the text by setting غليظ القلب as the direct opposite of لِنتَ (softness/gentleness). From this one physical notion the Quran extends the word to hearts and manners that will not soften (harsh/stern), and to a bond that will not break (a firm, solemn covenant). One extension — the fixed phrase عذاب غليظ (a 'grievous/heavy' punishment) — has no internal cue tying it back to non-softness and may simply be a lexicalized intensifier, so it is held apart as a resistant sub-class. This is why the account is graded MODERATE, not STRONG.
glZ.strongest_counterexample: عَذَاب غَلِيظ (11:58, 14:17, 31:24, 41:50) is a lexicalized collocation with no Quran-internal anchor tying it to non-softness; it reads plausibly as a generic 'severe/heavy' punishment, so its bridge to the density nucleus is inferred, not demonstrated. This is the resistant sub-class that caps the grade below STRONG. (Conversely, 48:29 — a healthy crop growing stout — is the decisive counterexample against the rival 'harshness/severity-first' core, since a plant stem cannot be harsh, only thick.)
glZ.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) converged on the density/non-softness nucleus, MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE, and distinctiveness from شِدَاد and فَظّ; they diverged only on which collocation is the resistant seam, reconciled here to عَذَاب غَلِيظ.

qnt.candidate_root_contribution: qnt = a durative, settled posture of obedient subordination / sustained availability directed to a sovereign authority — invariantly Allah in every explicit case (once jointly to Allah and His Messenger, 33:31). In rational agents this is realized as willed, humble, standing devotional obedience before God (prototypically prolonged standing/night-vigil prayer); in the totality of creation it is involuntary ontological subjection. The single core that survives all 13 is directional 'standing-under / at the disposal of the Sovereign', not any specific act.
qnt.plain_explanation: Across all 13 occurrences (one tight Form-I family: 11 active participles qānit/qānitūn/qānitīn/qānitāt plus the verb yaqnut and imperative uqnutī), qnt names being obediently subordinate and continually available to a higher authority, which internally is always God. Wherever an object is stated it is li-llāh / lahū / li-rabbi (16:120, 2:238, 3:43, 2:116, 30:26), extended only once to 'Allah and His Messenger' (33:31) and never to a purely human authority. In people this shows as sustained worshipful standing before God (39:9 through the watches of the night, 2:238 'stand for Allah qānitīn', 3:43 alongside but distinct from bowing and prostration), and as a named virtue-class among the righteous (33:35, 3:17, 66:5, 16:120, 66:12). But the same participle is predicated of all creation in 2:116 / 30:26 ('all are qānitūn to Him'), where it can only mean subjection, not chosen piety. The thin subordination sense bridges every case; the richer devotional content is representative of the human sub-set, not universal.
qnt.strongest_counterexample: 2:116:14:1 and its verbatim parallel 30:26:8:1 — كُلٌّ لَّهُۥ قَٰنِتُونَ predicates qnt of the totality of creation in the heavens and earth, including the very deniers 2:116 rebuts. This decisively falsifies any account that makes distinctive voluntary devout worship the root nucleus: rocks, skies and unbelievers cannot be devout. It forces the core down to involuntary universal subjection, showing the devotional richness of the human verses is contextually supplied, not lexical.
qnt.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A occurrence/directionality, B nucleus/derivation-family, C adversarial) converged on the same nucleus, the same resistant cosmic seam, and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE cap.

xzn.candidate_root_contribution: xzn contributes the holding of something in secured custody within a bounded, access-controlled enclosure, realized in two morphological faces: the patient/place face khaza'in (the reserve-repository held under exclusive or delegated ownership, from which content is released only in a controlled measure and which may be withheld) and the agent face khazin/khazana (the one who keeps such a bounded holding and governs its boundary). The distinctive core (secured reserve + metered/controlled release) is broad and adversarially clean across the store-class and its provision-keeper agent, but attenuates to bare custody-of-a-gated-enclosure in the khazana sub-class.
xzn.plain_explanation: Across 13 nominal occurrences the root splits by morphology into three faces of one custodial notion. The dominant broken plural khaza'in (8x) names God's (or, once, Egypt's) secured reserve-stores: what one owns and releases only 'in a known measure' (15:21) or could withhold rather than spend (17:100). The active participle khazinin (15:22) is the transparent agent of that same idea (humans are not the keepers/storers of the sky-water), welding the store to its keeper in one pericope (15:21-22). The agent-plural khazana (4x) are the angelic gate-custodians of Hell and the Garden, who open gates, interrogate, or welcome at the threshold but store and dispense nothing. The narrow, distinctive reserve/metered-release sense governs the first two faces (9/13); the khazana face requires retreating to the thinner, less distinctive 'custody of a gated enclosure', so it is carried as a coherent resistant sub-class rather than a live instance of the reserve-sense.
xzn.strongest_counterexample: 39:73:15:1 (khazanatuha of the Garden). These keepers hold no reserve, ration nothing in measure, and do not even interrogate for admission - they merely welcome ('salamun 'alaykum tibtum fadkhuluha'). The distinctive core (secured reserve dispensed by controlled measure) is fully bleached here, leaving only a bare attendant-at-the-gate. Even a 'guard against escape/confinement' reading fails, since these are ushers, not wardens. This anchors the khazana class as a resistant lexicalized custodial sub-class rather than a live realization of the reserve-sense.
xzn.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each read all 13, each partitioned the data identically into khaza'in / khazin / khazana, and each independently graded MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE with the khazana class as the resistant sub-class; the adversary's push toward a two-class split was tested and rejected only because of the 15:21-22 provision-keeper bridge.

E*r.candidate_root_contribution: The presentation or existence of a GROUND that would clear or release a party from blame or obligation (forensic exculpation / warrant of exemption). The derivational family distributes predictably from one nucleus: Form VIII اعتذر = the reflexive act of putting a self-clearing plea before an evaluating authority; مَعْذِرَة/مَعَاذِير = the act/instance and plural pleas; N(II) مُعَذِّرون = agents presenting excuses to obtain exemption; عُذْر = the exempting ground/warrant itself. The root carries no entailment of the plea's truth, its acceptance, or of pardon, and is categorically distinct from the near-homograph عذاب (root ع ذ ب).
E*r.plain_explanation: Every occurrence of ع ذ ر turns on offering, or possessing, a reason that would release someone from blame or an obligation. In the Form VIII verb it is the act of making excuses for oneself (uniformly forbidden, denied, or futile in-frame); in مَعْذِرَة/مَعَاذِير it is the plea/ground itself; in مُعَذِّرون it is the people making excuses to be exempted; in عُذْر it is the exempting ground or warrant. The Quran does not build the word to mean the excuse is true, accepted, or forgiven — that is always supplied by context, and belated self-clearing before God is consistently shown as unavailing.
E*r.strongest_counterexample: 18:76:13:1 «قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِن لَّدُنِّى عُذْرًا»: عذر here is an objectively-attained ground/warrant conceded by the offending party that entitles the OTHER party (Khidr) to part, not a self-exculpatory plea offered by a blameworthy party to a judge — inverting both the polarity (valid/effective, not a rejected plea) and the agent-direction of the dominant self-exculpation frame. It cannot be reduced to the Form-VIII plea sense and forces the root-level unifier up to the broader 'ground for release/exemption.'
E*r.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) converged on MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE and independently identified 18:76 (and 77:6) as the resistant nominal seam and 7:164 as the valid-discharge bridge datum.

Tyn.candidate_root_contribution: طين (ṭīn) is a single frozen nominal naming a concrete substance: moist, cohesive, moldable earthen matter (clay) functioning as the raw, pre-form source-material out of which shaped things are produced — a human/bashar, a bird-shape, fired bricks, or hardened projectile stones. It is a substance/source noun, never the finished artifact, and it is agent-, purpose-, and valence-neutral.
Tyn.plain_explanation: Every one of the 12 occurrences is the same noun ṭīn (only case/definiteness vary; no verb, participle, plural, or derived nominal exists). Across all of them the word points to the identical stuff: wet, workable, cohesive earth used as the material something is made FROM. What differs is supplied by the surrounding verbs and nouns (خلق 'create/shape', أوقد 'kindle/fire', أرسل 'send'; بشر, هيئة الطير, حجارة, صرح), not by ṭīn. The frequent 'man is made of clay' sense is therefore a property of the collocation khalaqa…min, not of the word: strip that collocation (Pharaoh firing clay into bricks, 28:38; stones of clay, 51:33) and ṭīn is bare industrial/earthen material. Because the root surfaces as only one lexeme with no derivational field, the 'unity' achieved is essentially the identity of a concrete mass noun, and its distinctiveness from other earth-creation terms cannot be tested here; hence a stable but modest result rather than a strong root-generalization.
Tyn.strongest_counterexample: 28:38 (Pharaoh: «فَأَوْقِدْ لِى يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلطِّينِ فَٱجْعَل لِّى صَرْحًا») together with 51:33 («حِجَارَةً مِّن طِينٍ») strip away every contextual halo — no creation, no divine agency, no life, no punishment-by-creation — leaving ṭīn as ordinary industrial/earthen material fired into bricks and constituting hard stones. These two tokens single-handedly disprove any 'creation/origin substance' nucleus: the origin-of-life reading in the other tokens comes from the verb خَلَقَ + مِن, not from ṭīn. They do not resist the bare-substance account; they confirm and broaden it while defeating the richer creation reading.
Tyn.independent_verification: Adversary Lens C independently confirmed the substance nucleus is adversarially clean across 12 tokens while capping the grade at MODERATE for monoformity and the collocational nature of the creation sense; Lens B independently flagged the turāb/ṣalṣāl distinctiveness sub-claim as UNRESOLVED on this evidence.

ZmA.candidate_root_contribution: ZmA denotes the bodily deprivation-state of lacking/needing water — thirst — oriented toward مَاء (water) as its object of relief. It is realized transparently across its derivational family: the imperfect verb (to be/become thirsty, 20:119), the فَعْلان state-adjective/participle (the thirsty one who bears the condition, 24:39), and the masdar (thirst as an endured affliction, 9:120). One physiological nucleus, no lexicalized second sense, no metaphorical migration of the lexeme itself.
ZmA.plain_explanation: Across all three Quranic occurrences the root means literal, bodily thirst — the felt lack of water. In Paradise the promise is that 'you will not thirst' (20:119); on campaign 'no thirst afflicts them' as a rewarded hardship (9:120); and 'the thirsty one' mistakes a mirage for water in the desert (24:39). The Quran itself fixes the object as water (مَاء in 24:39) and repeatedly lists thirst as a member distinct from hunger, fatigue, heat, and nakedness. The account is graded MODERATE only because the corpus is thin (3 tokens, the verb attested only under negation), not because any occurrence resists.
ZmA.strongest_counterexample: 24:39 (ٱلظَّمْـَٔانُ embedded in the mirage simile كَسَرَابٍ). Candidate reading: the root is deployed figuratively for illusion / false hope / the disbelievers' craving for reward. It fails: the ظمآن is himself literally thirsty and literally seeks water (يَحْسَبُهُ … مَآءً), and the metaphor operates at the level of the whole simile (deeds ≈ mirage), external to the lexeme. The strongest available counterexample exemplifies rather than resists the literal-water-thirst nucleus.
ZmA.independent_verification: Three independent analyses (A bottom-up, B top-down, C adversarial) converged on the same nucleus, boundaries, and the failure of the sole counterexample candidate.

fjj.candidate_root_contribution: fjj denotes an open, traversable passage/route through terrain (paradigmatically the earth's land, between anchoring mountains). It is a static geographic conduit for travel — realized as a discrete pass (sg. faj~, 22:27) and as such passes / the 'broad-open' quality of ways (pl. fijaAj, 21:31, 71:20). fjj supplies the notion of the passage itself and, as an attribute, its openness/breadth; it does NOT supply motion, the generic 'way/road' (subul, which it co-occurs with and modifies), nor any eventive 'splitting/opening'.
fjj.plain_explanation: Across all three attestations fjj is a concrete geographic word for an open way through the land that people travel by. It appears twice paired with the ordinary word for 'ways' (subul) — once as the noun 'passes' (21:31 'fijaAjan subulan') and once as the adjective 'broad' describing those ways (71:20 'subulan fijaAjan') — and once as a singular head-noun 'from every deep/remote faj' (22:27). The pairing with, and modification of, subul shows fjj is not merely a synonym for 'road': it is the open passage/route, or the broad-open quality of a route. The evidence is fully coherent but thin (3 tokens, purely noun/adjective, one physical domain, no verb).
fjj.strongest_counterexample: 22:27:13:1 'min kulli faj~in EamIqin' — the only singular, only non-subul-paired token, and the salient qualifier is EamIq ('deep/remote'), not width. Against any account that makes breadth CRITERIAL this resists: 'broad' does no work here. It is resolved by demoting breadth to a foregrounded-but-optional nuance (broad in 71:20, deep in 22:27) and setting the essential core at 'traversable open passage/route through terrain,' which 22:27 satisfies as a deep/remote pass. No occurrence resists that core.
fjj.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversarial C) converged on the same unified nucleus, the same distinctiveness argument from subul, the same two hard cases (22:27 breadth, 71:20 N/ADJ), and the same MODERATE + REPRESENTATIVE grade.

fzz.candidate_root_contribution: fzz (attested only as Form X, istafʿala) = a hostile agent's conative act of jolting/unsettling a settled personal target out of a stable position and driving it toward forced motion. The nature of the position is specified by the complement, not by the verb: spatial/territorial when مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ is present (17:103, 17:76), dispositional/moral when the instrument is a voice and no locative appears (17:64). It names the destabilizing attempt or pressure, never the accomplished displacement.
fzz.plain_explanation: In all three occurrences (all in Sūrah 17, all Form X), a hostile party works to shake a person loose from where they are settled and push them into motion. Twice this is 'from the land' (Pharaoh against Moses' people 17:103; the deniers against the Prophet 17:76), and once it is Satan stirring people toward sin 'with your voice' (17:64). The verb consistently marks the attempt/pressure, not the finished result — 17:76 even keeps it separate from the actual expulsion (لِيُخْرِجُوكَ) it aims to cause.
fzz.strongest_counterexample: 17:64:1:2 وَٱسْتَفْزِزْ ... بِصَوْتِكَ — the only occurrence with no territorial complement, a voice as instrument, and a target moved morally (toward going astray) rather than physically. It defeats any tight 'drive out of a place/expel' reading: whatever fzz means, it cannot lexically be spatial removal, since here there is no land and no 'from'. It is accommodated only by the broader 'forcefully unsettle a settled target into motion' nucleus, of which the spatial cases are the complement-specified subtype.
fzz.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each independently reached the same single-nucleus account and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade, each flagging 17:64 as the divergent-but-bridged sub-class.

jdv.candidate_root_contribution: A purely nominal, definite-plural lexeme (al-ajdāth) naming the bounded plural resting-container of the dead, profiled exclusively as the source-locus (always مِن-governed) FROM WHICH humans emerge at the resurrection. The root carries no verbal/eventive content and no attested singular; it names a place, never an act, and appears only as the origin-pole of eschatological egress, opposed to the destination-pole (ilā rabbihim / ilā nuṣub).
jdv.plain_explanation: In all three Quranic occurrences the root ج د ث shows up as exactly one word, ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ ('the ajdāth', plural), always after مِن ('from') and always with a verb of coming/hastening out (yansilūn, yakhrujūn) in a resurrection scene: people rush out of the ajdāth toward their Lord or toward a marker. So the root names the place the dead are held in and emerge from when raised. It is only ever a location one exits, never something one does, and never a place one goes to.
jdv.strongest_counterexample: None internal to the packet. All three tokens uniformly satisfy the account (same lexeme, same مِن-egress frame, same emergence verbs, same eschatological register); no occurrence resists. The nearest stress point, 70:43, might be read as a mustering-ground rather than a resting-place, but the min/ilā polarity (from ajdāth → to nuṣub) and the verb خرج shared with 54:7 pin it to the egress-origin reading. The cleanliness reflects homogeneity/formularity (54:7 ≈ 70:43 is a reused slot), not survival of diverse adversarial stress-tests.
jdv.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B, C adversarial) each independently reached the same single-class account and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE ceiling, and each independently flagged the qbr non-distinctiveness and low-diversity limitation.

l**.candidate_root_contribution: لذذ contributes consummated, recipient-relative sensory pleasure: the gratification a perceiving/consuming faculty realizes in a present object. The nominal laḏḏah names the object's pleasure-giving quality anchored to a recipient (li-l-šāribīn); the Form-I verb talaḏḏu names the faculty's own act of enjoying (al-aʿyun as subject). These are two diatheses of one pleasure-relation — source-is-pleasing / faculty-is-pleased. The nucleus is faculty-general (taste and sight both attested), always relational (never a perceiver-independent absolute property), and distinct from appetitive wanting.
l**.plain_explanation: In all three occurrences the root marks actual, enjoyed pleasure delivered to a person's sense-faculty by something present. Twice it is the noun laḏḏah ('a pleasure') predicated of a paradisiacal drink and pinned to its drinkers (37:46, 47:15); once it is the verb 'the eyes take pleasure' (43:71). The root does not mean the flavor of a drink specifically, nor the desire/craving that precedes enjoyment — 43:71 keeps laḏḏ (delighting) explicitly distinct from shahw (craving) in the same clause.
l**.strongest_counterexample: 43:71:11:2 «وَتَلَذُّ ٱلْأَعْيُنُ» ('and the eyes take pleasure'). It is the only verb, the only sight-modality token, and the only case where the faculty (al-aʿyun) is the grammatical experiencer rather than the pleasure being predicated of an object. It defeats any narrow 'delicious-drink' account by shifting modality (taste->sight), argument orientation (object-as-pleasure->faculty-as-experiencer), and form (nominal->finite verb). It does not break the unified account — it in fact confirms the faculty-general pleasure nucleus and, via the coordinated مَا تَشْتَهِيهِ ٱلْأَنفُسُ, supplies the sharpest internal distinction of laḏḏ (consummated pleasure) from shahw (appetitive craving). It disciplines how narrow the account may go without refuting it.
